name: Rampage

date.source: Month: the fed's own title-history pages date title changes to 'Rampage', 26 March 2006, but the PTC forum's own posts place the show earlier: a news post of 28 February 2006 puts Rampage “just two weeks away”, the card was posted on 11 March 2006, and the WorldWide 43 card posted on 22 March 2006 calls itself “The Aftermath of Rampage” and has Dawn McFarlane defending the World Championship that Rampage's main event was to decide. Danielle Northsky won by disqualification and remained Television Champion: as she and Jacob McKail (the “????” of the billing, the man who had just survived the Gauntlet) fought, a masked man who had lost to Shadow a few weeks earlier ran in with a chair and hit Northsky, and the referee called for the bell ('Your winner, as a result of a disqualification and STILL GCW Television Champion... DANIELLE NORTHSKY!'). Gray and Joshua Brand then ran in and drove the masked man off.

Billed on the card as “Seymour Almasy vs. Nerezza”. Seymour Almasy won, pinning Nerezza after a layout seated boot he calls Naught's Approach; the official raised his hand.

Valentine, at ringside with Ukyo Kushinaga holding Eva VanLorne, threw the towel into the ring so that the referee called for the bell ('The winner of this match... Blaise “Hazard” McClancy!').

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Dawn McFarlane vs. LeStatt Knight”. LeStatt Knight won the GCW World Heavyweight Championship from Dawn McFarlane with the KnightFall ('Here is your winner, and the NEWWWWWW GCW World Heavyweight Champion... LESTATT KNIGHT!!!').

notes: Also on the card: “Bryan Mayhem vs. Kaos”. No winner is declared. The bout, a Last Man Standing Match, never begins in the ring: Kaos finds Mayhem's casket empty, chases him backstage to the loading dock, and is beaten and chokeslammed there; Kaos's father clubs the referee, Kaos throws Mayhem into a trash compactor, and Mayhem seems to be crushed. Shadow then shakes Kaos's hand, Mayhem bursts out of a trailer, and Mayhem chains Kaos's neck, Almasy kicks Kaos's father down, and the two of them throw both men into the back of the truck, which Mayhem drives away; “Brandon Youngblood vs. Baltasar”. Brandon Youngblood won by submission, a katahajime (a rear choke) held after a katahajime suplex, and Baltasar tapped out. Afterwards Seymour Almasy came out and stood in the ring, clapping, while Youngblood stared back at him.

Khan pinned Finger Ninja (chair-assisted) first, then the Jhub second, then Toxic last (Phoenix Moonsault splash) to retain, and then relinquished the title in a post-match promo.

Billed on the card as “One Night Tournament, Round 1: Gigas vs. Octavian”. Octavian pinned Gigas with a schoolboy rollup, after Octavian worked over Gigas's knee.

Billed on the card as “CWU World Heavyweight Championship: "Blockbuster" Kurt Richards vs. Badger Benandanti”. Special guest referee Steven Caldera was knocked out by Badger (Badgerslam); a masked "Netheradege" (revealed as Sexual Inferno) and "The Renegade" (revealed as Rich Rollins) interfered on opposite sides, and Rollins used Caldera's unconscious hand to count the winning pin for Badger Benandanti, who retained.

The belt is the predecessor company CWU's own, not GCW's Cruiserweight championship (GCW's own lineage begins with Chameleon's win at Warpath on 22 April 2001, three months after this card), so the row carries no GCW title. Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy climbed and unhooked the belt to win over Chameleon, Skyy, Bill Banse and Dark Wolf; Outlaw Kid was jumped backstage before the bell and interfered late but never legally entered; “The General vs. Alpha”. The General pinned Alpha with a move he calls "the Court-martial."; “CWU World Heavyweight Championship: "Blockbuster" Kurt Richards vs. Badger Benandanti”. The belt is the predecessor company CWU's own, not GCW's World Heavyweight championship (GCW's own lineage begins with Octavian's win at Warpath on 22 April 2001), so the row carries no GCW title. Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy ran in from the crowd and chaired Chameleon (co-holder of the Tag Team titles and the Cruiserweight champion) just before the final turnbuckle, letting Zippy finish uncontested and win the $1,000,000 prize. Zippy and Chameleon each had a second at ringside who took no action in the bout (Zippy's, billed only as “Stone”; Chameleon's, Jack Pott); “GCW Hardcore Championship: Toad vs. John Reed”. Post-match, three unnamed men jumped the guardrail and joined Dream in a four-on-one beatdown of Krowe; “Number One Contender's Match: The Jhub vs. Toxic”. Champion Rollins retained, superkicking a chair Shane Lane swung at him back into Shane Lane's own face for the pin, after Commissioner Mr. Danger's chair swing at Shane Lane (meant to even out Hiroshima Genryu's own interference) hit Rollins by mistake and nearly cost him the title. Post-match, Shane Lane ambushed the still-recovering Rollins with a Superstar Slam; this had no bearing on the already-decided result.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship: Chameleon vs. Chris Jordan”. Challenger Chameleon reversed champion Chris Jordan's attempted Canadian Suplex (off the top rope onto four chairs) into a tornado DDT onto the chairs for the pin, becoming new Hardcore champion; Chris Jordan simultaneously held the Cruiserweight title into this match, which stayed on him.

Billed on the card as “The Jhub vs. John Reed”. The Jhub won by a second Sharpshooter, knocking John Reed unconscious. Khan chaired the Jhub from behind immediately after the bell, unrelated to the match's own result.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Shane Lane vs. Octavian (mystery challenger)”. President Caldera, also returning, fired Mr. Danger as Commissioner on the spot and installed Octavian in the role. No bell, pinfall or formal decision closes the match;

notes: Also on the card: “Katanya vs. Icebabe”. Katanya won, reversing an Icebabe hurricanrana attempt into a powerbomb; “GCW Hardcore Championship: Chameleon vs. Chris Jordan”. Challenger Chameleon reversed champion Chris Jordan's attempted Canadian Suplex (off the top rope onto four chairs) into a tornado DDT onto the chairs for the pin, becoming new Hardcore champion; Jordan simultaneously held the Cruiserweight title into this match, which stayed on him; “The Jhub vs. John Reed”. The Jhub won by a second Sharpshooter, knocking Reed unconscious. Khan chaired the Jhub from behind immediately after the bell, unrelated to the match's own result; “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Shane Lane vs. Octavian (mystery challenger)”. No result: the referee was knocked out by a collision caused by Shane Lane before Shane Lane's Superstar Slam could be counted, and the match was left permanently unresolved. Returning Commissioner-hopeful Mr. Danger ran in, Octavian grabbed champion Shane Lane's own title belt intending to hit him with it but Shane Lane ducked and it struck Danger instead, and Shane Lane and Octavian then jointly beat Danger down. President Caldera, also returning, fired Danger as Commissioner on the spot and installed Octavian in the role. No bell, pinfall or formal decision closes the match; Shane Lane's championship is not recorded as changing hands here.

name: Meltdown 21

date.source: Circa 8 August 2001 (window 8 to 9 August): the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 8 August 2001, and its United States title history dates Tristain Mayhem's win of that title on a Meltdown, staged on this card, to 9 August 2001.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW United States Championship: Tristain Mayhem vs. The Jhub”. Champion the Jhub had Mayhem tapping to a Sharpshooter, but the referee was down (accidentally struck by Mayhem earlier); CWU's Rich Rollins ran in and superkicked the Jhub, and a revived referee counted Mayhem's pin, crowning a new champion.

Billed on the card as “John Reed, "The Fueler" Luke Hanson & Octavian vs. Eric "All That" Allen, "Blockbuster" Kurt Richards & Rich "The Renegade" Rollins”. The returning ACWF (Mr. Danger, Big Daddy Dero and Mangler) ran in and attacked both teams, and the referee called for the bell; no winner is announced. Danger then challenged GCW and the CWU to a three-team WarGames match at the (as-yet-undated) Heatwave, joined by a fourth man, the Heckler, who also ran in on the ACWF's side. Kurt Richards notably refused to cheat, breaking up his own side's double-team on Octavian and staying on the apron until legally tagged. none of Allen, Richards, Dero, Mangler or the Heckler has one.
Billed on the card as “Toxic vs. Shane Lane”. Toxic's own text describes him newly turning on GCW as of the prior Oblivion.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-cruiserweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Cruiserweight Championship: Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy vs. Chris Jordan”. Mike Hardy won with a schoolboy rollup, becoming new Cruiserweight champion.

notes: Also on the card: “Toxic vs. Shane Lane”. Toxic, newly aligned with the CWU, won with the Toxic Waste after CWU's Eric Allen ran in and distracted Shane Lane at the ropes just after Shane Lane's own Superstar Slam. Toxic's own text describes him newly turning on GCW as of the prior Oblivion; “Women's Battle Royal”. Five entrants (Katanya, Icebabe, Emma, Bridget, Gidget). Bridget was eliminated first, dropkicked out by Katanya; Icebabe then lifted Katanya, Emma and Gidget together and dumped all three over the top rope at once to win outright and become the first GCW Women's Champion. Post-match, the four losers (billed collectively elsewhere as the ‘Cherry Bombs’) ambushed Icebabe -- Emma clotheslined her and Katanya powerbombed her -- with no bearing on the already-decided title change. (The fed's own Women's title history names Katanya, not Icebabe, as the belt's first billed champion; Gidget is billed champion on Meltdown 24, 10 July 2001. The readings disagree and both stand.); “GCW Cruiserweight Championship: Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy vs. Chris Jordan”. Hardy won with a schoolboy rollup, becoming new Cruiserweight champion.

name: Meltdown 23

date.source: Circa: this card previews Heatwave (20 August 2001 in the fed's own title histories), and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 16 August 2001.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight & Tristain Mayhem vs. the Sick Freaks (X-Caliber & Dimensioner)”. LeStatt Knight repeatedly refused to tag his own partner Tristain Mayhem, who took a long beating before finally forcing a tag; Knight then re-entered arguing with Mayhem and was caught by Dimensioner with a powerbomb for the pin. X-Caliber is Dimensioner's partner.

Billed on the card as “John Reed vs. Luke Hanson”. World Champion Rich Rollins sat in on commentary. John Reed countered Luke Hanson's underhook powerbomb attempt into a Cradle Tombstone for the pin; Rollins then entered the ring and chair-shotted both men ahead of defending his title against John Reed.

Billed on the card as “Dan Rivero vs. Iron Mike Lindsay”. Dan Rivero countered a top-rope cross body with a dropkick, then hit the Rivero elbow for the pin over Iron Mike Lindsay. Afterward, the Heckler ran in and beat Rivero down; the two are booked for Zippy's TV title at Heatwave.
Billed on the card as “Katanya vs. Emma”. A #1-contendership match for a shot at Gidget's title; Katanya beat Emma clean with a super hurricanrana from the top rope.
Billed on the card as “JNightmare vs. Eric Allen”. In his GCW debut, JNightmare rolled up Eric Allen for the upset pin after Allen was distracted by System-X walking to ringside.

notes: Also on the card: “Dan Rivero vs. Iron Mike Lindsay”. Dan Rivero countered a top-rope cross body with a dropkick, then hit the Rivero elbow for the pin over Iron Mike Lindsay. Afterward, the Heckler ran in and beat Rivero down; the two are booked for Zippy's TV title at Heatwave; “JNightmare vs. Eric Allen”. In his GCW debut, JNightmare rolled up Eric Allen for the upset pin after Allen was distracted by System-X walking to ringside; “Katanya vs. Emma”. A #1-contendership match for a shot at Gidget's title; Katanya beat Emma clean with a super hurricanrana from the top rope; “John Reed vs. Luke Hanson”. World Champion Rich Rollins sat in on commentary. John Reed countered Luke Hanson's underhook powerbomb attempt into a Cradle Tombstone for the pin; Rollins then entered the ring and chair-shotted both men ahead of defending his title against Reed.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship, Steel Cage: Toad vs. Jason Dread”. While both men were down mid-brawl, TV champion Dan Rivero climbed the cage from outside and hit a Rivero Elbow on champion Dread; Toad then simply crawled out the door to win the title for a fourth time (a cage match here wins by escape, not pinfall). Rivero's interference helped Toad only incidentally -- he targeted Dread, not Toad, and left before Toad exited.

Billed on the card as “Rich "The Renegade" Rollins & Octavian vs. Tristain Mayhem & John Reed”. Mayhem pinned Octavian (not the legal man, whom Mayhem hit with a leaping DDT, ‘Hammer On,’ breaking up a Roman Rapper on the unconscious John Reed) for the win; John Reed's World Heavyweight Championship was not at stake.

Billed on the card as “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. JNightmare”. Ruled a win for Hanson by disqualification after LeStatt Knight (recently returned from a Heatwave injury) ran in and chop-blocked Hanson from behind for no stated reason.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Stone”. Champion Rivero retained, hitting a top-rope Rivero Elbow after the referee had been knocked down. Stone is billed here as an eWa member; the text gives no fuller name.
Billed on the card as “Dimensioner & X-Caliber (the Sick Freaks) vs. Big Daddy Dero & the Heckler (the cOd)”. The Heckler won for the cOd with a top-rope powerbomb (‘the Final Insult’) on X-Caliber.

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 11 July 2001; the card's own text dates it 6 September 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “GCW Television Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Stone”. Champion Rivero retained, hitting a top-rope Rivero Elbow after the referee had been knocked down. Stone is billed here as an eWa member; the text gives no fuller name; “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. JNightmare”. Ruled a win for Hanson by disqualification after LeStatt Knight (recently returned from a Heatwave injury) ran in and chop-blocked Hanson from behind for no stated reason; “Dimensioner & X-Caliber (the Sick Freaks) vs. Big Daddy Dero & the Heckler (the cOd)”. The Heckler won for the cOd with a top-rope powerbomb (‘the Final Insult’) on X-Caliber.

name: Meltdown 26

date.source: Circa: this card opens with scenes from the previous week's Meltdown, which the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) dates 30 August 2001, and the list lists the next Meltdown on 6 September 2001.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Non-Title Match: Jason Dread vs. Tristain Mayhem”. Dread won by count-out after knocking Mayhem into a ringside Rich Rollins, sparking a Mayhem/Rollins brawl that kept Mayhem outside the ring past the referee's ten count.

Billed on the card as “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. Octavian”. Octavian held a figure-four on Hanson's leg around the ring post past the referee's own ten-count, and the bell rang mid-hold; the broadcast team only speculates that this goes to Hanson (‘I think this match is going to Hanson’) and no formal winner is ever announced on-page, so the result is left unresolved rather than guessed. Octavian then chaired Hanson's knee repeatedly, and separately chaired and Roman-Rappered the arriving the Jhub (recovering from knee surgery, not a competitor in this match), unrelated to any decision in the match itself.
Billed on the card as “Big Skails vs. Great Tiger”. Tiger won with a top-rope moonsault.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. John Reed”. Champion Reed retained with a Cradle Tombstone on Rivero after a chaotic finish: Octavian ran in and Roman-Rappered Reed (unrelated to the eventual pin), Jason Dread ran in and hit Rivero with a Tres Flores (cobra clutch bulldog) in revenge for an earlier Rivero attack, and a debuting Rich Sherwin ran in and chaired Dread to protect Rivero -- the referee was down for most of this and revived just in time to count John Reed's final pin on Rivero.

Billed on the card as “Cage Match: Big Daddy Dero vs. President Steven Caldera”. Dero was nearly out the door when Mr. Danger ran in from the crowd and slammed the cage door on his skull, then beat him down inside the cage while Caldera climbed out over the top to win.

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 12 July 2001; the card's own text dates it 13 September 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “Big Skails vs. Great Tiger”. Tiger won with a top-rope moonsault; “Cage Match: Big Daddy Dero vs. President Steven Caldera”. Dero was nearly out the door when Mr. Danger ran in from the crowd and slammed the cage door on his skull, then beat him down inside the cage while Caldera climbed out over the top to win; “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. John Reed”. Champion Reed retained with a Cradle Tombstone on Rivero after a chaotic finish: Octavian ran in and Roman-Rappered Reed (unrelated to the eventual pin), Jason Dread ran in and hit Rivero with a Tres Flores (cobra clutch bulldog) in revenge for an earlier Rivero attack, and a debuting Rich Sherwin ran in and chaired Dread to protect Rivero -- the referee was down for most of this and revived just in time to count Reed's final pin on Rivero.

name: Meltdown 27

matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Commissionership Match: Octavian vs. The Jhub”. Champion (Commissioner) Octavian worked over the Jhub's surgically repaired knee and hit a Roman Devastator, but World Champion John Reed then ran in and guillotined Octavian over the top rope; the Jhub followed with a Downward Spiral and pinned Octavian to become the new Commissioner. A pre-match brawl on this same card (System-X ambushed by the Sick Freaks, JNightmare and Twisted -- a group calling itself ‘the Militia’ -- before any bell rang for their own scheduled tag match) is a brawl, not a bout: no contest was ever underway.

Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. JNightmare”. Nightmare won with a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’) after Luke Hanson, ringside, distracted LeStatt Knight at the decisive moment; this set up a confirmed scaffold match between LeStatt Knight and Hanson at FallOut.
Billed on the card as “Capo vs. Lance Star”. Lance Star won with a corkscrew legdrop after reversing a Capo powerbomb attempt.

Billed on the card as “Jason Dread vs. Rich Sherwin”. Dread won by submission with the No Moment, after Sherwin's own spinning piledriver (‘the Shattered Reality’) onto a chair failed to put him away.
Billed on the card as “Twisted vs. Maverick Manson”. Manson's debut. He won with a Russian neck drop (‘the Sweet Kiss Goodnight’).

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 13 July 2001; the card's own text dates it 20 September 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “Twisted vs. Maverick Manson”. Manson's debut. He won with a Russian neck drop (‘the Sweet Kiss Goodnight’); “LeStatt Knight vs. JNightmare”. Nightmare won with a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’) after Luke Hanson, ringside, distracted Knight at the decisive moment; this set up a confirmed scaffold match between Knight and Hanson at FallOut; “Capo vs. Lance Star”. Star won with a corkscrew legdrop after reversing a Capo powerbomb attempt; “Jason Dread vs. Rich Sherwin”. Dread won by submission with the No Moment, after Sherwin's own spinning piledriver (‘the Shattered Reality’) onto a chair failed to put him away.

name: Meltdown 28

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Luke Hanson, John Reed & Tristain Mayhem vs. Rich "The Renegade" Rollins, LeStatt Knight & Octavian”. Reed rolled up and pinned Octavian for the win after a chaotic multi-man brawl (Knight and Hanson fought to the back without returning; Rollins and Octavian double-teamed Mayhem before Mayhem broke it up with a Hammer On on Rollins).

Billed on the card as “Lance Star vs. Chris Edge”. Lance Star rolled Edge up from behind and scrambled out of the ring, stealing the win while a ringside Adam Hartman needled Edge into repeated distraction; this booked Hartman against Edge at FallOut.
Billed on the card as “Twisted & JNightmare (the Lost Soul Militia) vs. Stewart Hix & Sherman Hix”. Nightmare pinned Stewart Hix with a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’).

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship: Toad vs. X-Caliber”. Champion Toad retained with a Toad Jam. A large brawl broke out mid-match between System-X (Hanson, Hardy) and the rest of the Lost Soul Militia (Dimensioner, Twisted, JNightmare) at ringside, ending with the Militia driven off; it did not change the bout's own outcome between Toad and X-Caliber.
Billed on the card as “Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Maverick Manson”. Champion (of the TV title, not defended here) Rivero won with a second Rivero Elbow.

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 14 July 2001; the card's own text dates it 27 September 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “Lance Star vs. Chris Edge”. Star rolled Edge up from behind and scrambled out of the ring, stealing the win while a ringside Adam Hartman needled Edge into repeated distraction; this booked Hartman against Edge at FallOut; “Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Maverick Manson”. Champion (of the TV title, not defended here) Rivero won with a second Rivero Elbow; “Twisted & JNightmare (the Lost Soul Militia) vs. Stewart Hix & Sherman Hix”. Nightmare pinned Stewart Hix with a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’); “GCW Hardcore Championship: Toad vs. X-Caliber”. Champion Toad retained with a Toad Jam. A large brawl broke out mid-match between System-X (Hanson, Hardy) and the rest of the Lost Soul Militia (Dimensioner, Twisted, JNightmare) at ringside, ending with the Militia driven off; it did not change the bout's own outcome between Toad and X-Caliber.

name: Meltdown 29

date.source: Circa: this card follows FallOut (30 September 2001 in the fed's own title histories, a pay-per-view date that may be the announced one), and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 11 October 2001, the first it carries after FallOut.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-tag-team
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Tag Team Championship: Toad & "The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. Twisted & Jason O'Neil (the Lost Soul Militia)”. New champions Twisted and O'Neil (billed here under a new name, the commentary catching itself mid-sentence correcting ‘JNightmare’ to ‘Jason O'Neil’ -- the same performer) won when Mike Hardy, trying to help System-X against interfering Sick Freaks (Dimensioner, X-Caliber), accidentally chaired champion Toad by mistake; Twisted covered for the pin. Post-match, an enraged Toad and Hanson beat Hardy down themselves (DeFueler, Toad Jam), apparently expelling him from the group.

Billed on the card as “Rich "The Renegade" Rollins vs. Jason Dread”. A returning masked man interfered against Rollins with a fisherman's DDT and unmasked as Badger Benandanti, his GCW debut; Dread then locked on the No Moment for the submission win.
Billed on the card as “Capo vs. Jeff Wylde”. Lance Star ran in with a lead pipe and beat down both men before either could win; no bell or formal decision closes the match in the text.

Billed on the card as “Lance Star vs. Biggs”. Lance Star feigned a back injury (even riding an EMT stretcher) to lure a sportsmanlike Biggs into helping him up, then hit a corkscrew legdrop (‘the Lance Star Sizzler’) for the pin.
Billed on the card as “Toxic vs. Sherman Hix”. Toxic's return match, won with the Toxic Waste.

notes: Also on the card: “Capo vs. Jeff Wylde”. Lance Star ran in with a lead pipe and beat down both men before either could win; no bell or formal decision closes the match in the text. Jeff Wylde has none; “Lance Star vs. Biggs”. Star feigned a back injury (even riding an EMT stretcher) to lure a sportsmanlike Biggs into helping him up, then hit a corkscrew legdrop (‘the Star Sizzler’) for the pin; “Toxic vs. Sherman Hix”. Toxic's return match, won with the Toxic Waste.

name: Meltdown 32

date.source: Circa: this card opens on 'last Sunday night' Devil's Night (28 October 2001 in the fed's own title histories), and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 1 November 2001.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti & The Jhub vs. Octavian & Jason Dread”. A returning Rich Rollins, sitting ringside and refusing to say which side he supported, superkicked the Jhub as he set up a Downward Spiral on Octavian, letting Octavian pin him; Rollins then openly aligned with Octavian and Dread. World Heavyweight Championship not at stake.
Billed on the card as “Shane Sanders vs. Biggs”. Biggs won with a rollup right after Sanders shoved the referee.

Billed on the card as “Chris Edge vs. Chameleon”. Chameleon's return match, won with a reverse DDT/DVD he calls ‘the Strike.’ A chaotic Cruiserweight-contenders brawl surrounded the match throughout (Chris Jordan, Lance Star and Capo all interfered against Chameleon; Michael Hardy, on commentary, ultimately came to Chameleon's defense against all three), none of it changing the pinfall itself; the two reconciled and allied afterward.

Billed on the card as “Twisted vs. Natural Born Killer”. Ruled a win for NBK (debuting the pairing ‘Simply Perfect’ with Dan Rivero and Angela Hatheway) by disqualification after an unidentified masked man interfered against NBK with a leg drop, letting Twisted hit a reverse DDT; the masked man fled before being identified.

notes: Also on the card: “Shane Sanders vs. Biggs”. Biggs won with a rollup right after Sanders shoved the referee; “Chris Edge vs. Chameleon”. Chameleon's return match, won with a reverse DDT/DVD he calls ‘the Strike.’ A chaotic Cruiserweight-contenders brawl surrounded the match throughout (Chris Jordan, Lance Star and Capo all interfered against Chameleon; Michael Hardy, on commentary, ultimately came to Chameleon's defense against all three), none of it changing the pinfall itself; the two reconciled and allied afterward. the other three do not; “Twisted vs. Natural Born Killer”. Ruled a win for NBK (debuting the pairing ‘Simply Perfect’ with Dan Rivero and Angela Hatheway) by disqualification after an unidentified masked man interfered against NBK with a leg drop, letting Twisted hit a reverse DDT; the masked man fled before being identified.

name: Meltdown 33

date.source: Circa: this card promotes NC-17 (25 November 2001 in the card's own text) and refers back to the previous week's card, and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 8 November 2001.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jason Dread vs. The Jhub”. Ruled a win for the Jhub by disqualification after Badger Benandanti ran in with a BadgerSlam on Dread, and then Rich Rollins pulled the referee out of the ring and decked him during the Jhub's legal cover. A post-match brawl (Octavian ran in for Dread/Rollins; Tristain Mayhem ran in against Octavian) had no bearing on the already-decided DQ. Rich Rollins does not.

Billed on the card as “Tristain Mayhem vs. Rich "The Renegade" Rollins”. Mayhem won clean with a small package after reversing a Rollins cover attempt, despite Octavian having chaired Mayhem from ringside earlier in the match (Mayhem kicked out of the resulting Rollins cover). Post-match, Octavian and Rollins jointly assaulted Mayhem with a Roman Rapper, restating on-mic that Nanci's child is Octavian's; this did not affect the already-decided result.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-womens
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Women's Championship: Katanya vs. the Grim Reaper”. GCW debut of the Grim Reaper (Lost Soul Militia), who won the title outright with a powerslam.

Billed on the card as “Zippy (and his Skeletal Finger Light Glove) vs. Gidget (and her Freddy Kruger Glove)”. A comedy gimmick match, both siblings wrestling wearing a novelty glove. Zippy's own glove landed on top of Gidget's when both gloves came off mid-move, and the referee counted the pin on that basis.
Billed on the card as “Icebabe vs. Angela Hathaway”. Hathaway (of Simply Perfect) won with a spike piledriver after NBK, at ringside, shoved Icebabe off the top rope.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Jason O'Neil”. The card's own text names the challenger ‘Reaper’ in its opening sentence but calls him ‘O'Neil’ throughout the rest of the summary; read as a single naming slip rather than two separate opponents, since only one challenger is ever actually described wrestling. Champion Rivero retained after Lance Star (revealed here as a new ally of Rivero's group, Simply Perfect) hit O'Neil with a Star Sizzler and rolled Rivero on top for the pin. A masked interferer helping the Lost Soul Militia (Twisted, the Grim Reaper) was unmasked afterward as ‘Misdirection.’

notes: Also on the card: “Zippy (and his Skeletal Finger Light Glove) vs. Gidget (and her Freddy Kruger Glove)”. A comedy gimmick match, both siblings wrestling wearing a novelty glove. Zippy's own glove landed on top of Gidget's when both gloves came off mid-move, and the referee counted the pin on that basis; “Icebabe vs. Angela Hathaway”. Hathaway (of Simply Perfect) won with a spike piledriver after NBK, at ringside, shoved Icebabe off the top rope; “GCW Women's Championship: Katanya vs. the Grim Reaper”. GCW debut of the Grim Reaper (Lost Soul Militia), who won the title outright with a powerslam. The in-ring result stands, but President Caldera stripped the belt back off the Reaper in a backstage segment immediately afterward, ruling a man of his size unfit to hold a women's title, and returned it to Katanya -- an administrative reversal by presidential authority, not a second match; “GCW Television Championship: Dan "The Man" Rivero vs. Jason O'Neil”. The card's own text names the challenger ‘Reaper’ in its opening sentence but calls him ‘O'Neil’ throughout the rest of the summary; read as a single naming slip rather than two separate opponents, since only one challenger is ever actually described wrestling. Champion Rivero retained after Lance Star (revealed here as a new ally of Rivero's group, Simply Perfect) hit O'Neil with a Star Sizzler and rolled Rivero on top for the pin. Lance Star and Misdirection do not, so neither gets an angle appearance row here.

name: Meltdown 30

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet (Toxic faces four opponents in succession)
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Gauntlet Match, leg 2: Toxic vs. Dimensioner”. Toxic won with the Toxic Waste.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet (Toxic faces four opponents in succession)
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Gauntlet Match, leg 3: Toxic vs. Jason O'Neil”. Ruled a win for Toxic by disqualification after O'Neil put him through the ringside announce table with a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’) before the bell had even restarted the leg -- the finish itself came post-bell/pre-restart, so it counted as a DQ rather than a fall.

Billed on the card as “Luke Hanson & Toad vs. Michael Hardy & Badger Benandanti”. Ruled a win for Hardy and Badger by disqualification when Hanson chaired Badger. A large brawl followed (Toxic and Tristain Mayhem ran in for Hardy/Badger's side; Octavian ran in and put a Roman Rapper on Badger), none of it bearing on the already-decided DQ result. This was also Badger Benandanti's first GCW in-ring appearance since his debut run-in the prior week.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: Sherman Hix vs. Jason Dread”. Champion Dread retained by submission with the No Moment.

Billed on the card as “Triple Threat No-DQ Match: Jeff Wylde vs. Capo vs. Lance Star”. Wylde won with a powerbomb (‘the Wylde Ride’) on Capo after Capo threw powder in Lance Star's eyes; Capo and Lance Star had briefly allied against Wylde mid-match before turning back on each other.

matches.stipulation: Gauntlet (Toxic faces four opponents in succession)
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Gauntlet Match, leg 1: Toxic vs. X-Caliber”. Toxic won with a new move, a jumping DDT he calls ‘the Black Hole.’

Billed on the card as “Gauntlet Match, leg 4: Toxic vs. Twisted”. Twisted won the gauntlet outright after Luke Hanson ran in, hit Toxic with a DeFueler, and dragged Twisted on top for the pin the distracted referee counted; Jason O'Neil had already been distracting the referee for a legitimate near-fall just before Hanson's run-in. Post-match, Toxic brawled with Hanson at ringside.
Billed on the card as “Natural Born Killer vs. Steve Johnston”. NBK won with a powerbomb (‘the 38 Special’).

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 5 October 2001; the card's own text dates it 18 October 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “GCW Television Championship: Sherman Hix vs. Jason Dread”. Champion Dread retained by submission with the No Moment; “Natural Born Killer vs. Steve Johnston”. NBK won with a powerbomb (‘the 38 Special’); “Triple Threat No-DQ Match: Jeff Wylde vs. Capo vs. Lance Star”. Wylde won with a powerbomb (‘the Wylde Ride’) on Capo after Capo threw powder in Lance Star's eyes; Capo and Star had briefly allied against Wylde mid-match before turning back on each other. Jeff Wylde and Lance Star have none; “Gauntlet Match, leg 1: Toxic vs. X-Caliber”; “Gauntlet Match, leg 4: Toxic vs. Twisted”. Twisted won the gauntlet outright after Luke Hanson ran in, hit Toxic with a DeFueler, and dragged Twisted on top for the pin the distracted referee counted; Jason O'Neil had already been distracting the referee for a legitimate near-fall just before Hanson's run-in. Post-match, Toxic brawled with Hanson at ringside.

name: Meltdown 31

matches.note: Billed on the card as “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. The Jhub”. The Jhub's return match, won with a top-rope Downward Spiral after Toxic ran in and chaired Hanson's back to prevent a top-rope DeFueler.

Billed on the card as “Non-Title Match: Octavian vs. Badger Benandanti”. Ruled a count-out win for Badger after Tristain Mayhem ran in and bulldogged Octavian from behind, sending him to the floor; the referee's count ran out with Octavian still outside.

Billed on the card as “Toxic vs. Natural Born Killer”. An upset: Luke Hanson ran in and hit champion (US title, not defended here) Toxic with a DeFueler after Toxic had slingshotted NBK into the referee, and NBK covered for the pin. This booked Hanson and Toxic in a barbed wire match at Devil's Night.

Billed on the card as “Twisted vs. Tristain Mayhem”. Ruled a win for Tristain Mayhem by disqualification after ‘The Dark Messiah’ Jason O'Neil hit Tristain Mayhem from behind during a legitimate cover on Twisted. Post-match, O'Neil hit Tristain Mayhem with a ‘Repentance’ and then a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’) through a ringside table, in what a backstage scene earlier in the show and a ringside exchange with Octavian afterward frame as a paid hit; O'Neil raised Twisted's hand afterward. Octavian then piledrove Nanci Schlatter, Mayhem's fiancée, in the ring -- an angle, not a match appearance.
Billed on the card as “Scotty Michaels vs. The Shocka”. Shocka won with an inside cradle after a low blow.

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 6 October 2001; the card's own text dates it 24 October 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “Scotty Michaels vs. The Shocka”. Shocka won with an inside cradle after a low blow; “Toxic vs. Natural Born Killer”. This booked Hanson and Toxic in a barbed wire match at Devil's Night; “Twisted vs. Tristain Mayhem”. Ruled a win for Mayhem by disqualification after ‘The Dark Messiah’ Jason O'Neil hit Mayhem from behind during a legitimate cover on Twisted. Post-match, O'Neil hit Mayhem with a ‘Repentance’ and then a full-nelson slam (‘the Recurring Nightmare’) through a ringside table, in what a backstage scene earlier in the show and a ringside exchange with Octavian afterward frame as a paid hit; O'Neil raised Twisted's hand afterward. Octavian then piledrove Nanci Schlatter, Mayhem's fiancée, in the ring -- an angle, not a match appearance.

name: Meltdown 45

date.source: The fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 7 February 2002, and its Television title history dates the title change staged on this card to the same day.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Demented”. Demented pinned LeStatt Knight with the Strike after Knight's own arm, worked over all match, gave out on a lifting attempt.
Billed on the card as “Toad vs. Toxic”. Toad caught Toxic coming off the ropes with a Toad Slam for the pin.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship: Luke Hanson vs. Badger Benandanti”. Badger Benandanti became the NEW GCW Hardcore Champion, pinning champion Luke Hanson with a springboard moonsault moments after former champion Toad ran in and hit Hanson with an unsanctioned Toad Jam, in payback for Hanson having taken the Hardcore title from Toad at Rampage.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: The Evangelist vs. Jeff Wylde”. The Evangelist took a steel chair from champion Jeff Wylde and used it to become the NEW GCW Television Champion with a reverse DDT onto the chair itself.

Billed on the card as “GCW Commissionership Match: Pete vs. Michael Stevens”. Pete was named the new GCW Commissioner after NBK ran in and hit Michael Stevens with the 38 Special, then coerced the official into counting Pete's pin over the incapacitated Michael Stevens. President Steven Caldera had set the stipulation match up hoping Michael Stevens would win it.

Billed on the card as “Non-Title: NBK vs. Jason Dread”. World Heavyweight Champion Jason Dread beat United States Champion NBK with a Tres Flores after Michael Stevens chair-shotted NBK from the floor; no title changed hands (non-title match).

notes: Also on the card: “GCW Television Championship: The Evangelist vs. Jeff Wylde”. The Evangelist took a steel chair from champion Jeff Wylde and used it to become the NEW GCW Television Champion with a reverse DDT onto the chair itself; “GCW Commissionership Match: Pete vs. Michael Stevens”. Pete was named the new GCW Commissioner after NBK ran in and hit Michael Stevens with the 38 Special, then coerced the official into counting Pete's pin over the incapacitated Stevens. President Steven Caldera had set the stipulation match up hoping Stevens would win it; “Non-Title: NBK vs. Jason Dread”. World Heavyweight Champion Jason Dread beat United States Champion NBK with a Tres Flores after Michael Stevens chair-shotted NBK from the floor; no title changed hands (non-title match).

name: Meltdown 47

date.source: Circa 21 February 2002 (window 20 to 21 February): this card opens four days before SubZero 'this Sunday' (24 February 2002 in the fed's own United States and Television title histories), and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 21 February 2002.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Triple Threat: Capo vs. Jeff Wylde vs. Jason O'Neil”. Jason O'Neil, entering battered and barely able to walk, threw no offense of his own beyond a boot to Capo; he then dragged Jeff Wylde on top of the fallen Capo for the pin, giving Wylde the win. After the match, Payne (Alex Grey) attacked the departing O'Neil, hitting a Lesson in Payne on the steel stage and throwing him off it through a table; O'Neil was taken out on a stretcher.

Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti & NBK vs. Michael Stevens & Toxic”. The Establishment's Michael Stevens and Toxic beat Badger Benandanti and United States Champion NBK -- Toxic hit NBK with two Toxic Wastes, then Stevens covered with an Inferno DDT for the pin after Toxic tossed Badger out to stop the save.

notes: Unlisted bout: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: Demented vs. The Evangelist”. The Evangelist retained the GCW Television Championship over Demented, catching him in mid-air off a reversed hurricanrana attempt and powerbombing him for the pin. Afterward, Jeff Wylde ran in from the crowd and destroyed both men and the ringside officials with a chair, over Commissioner Pete's $100,000 bounty on his head, before torching Pete's office.

name: Meltdown 48

date.source: Circa: this card opens 'four nights' after SubZero (24 February 2002 in the fed's own United States and Television title histories), and the fed's own Meltdown archive list (captured 16 October 2002) lists a Meltdown on 28 February 2002.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship: Toxic vs. Badger Benandanti”. Badger Benandanti retained the Hardcore title, making Toxic tap to the BadgerClutch after a falls-count-anywhere brawl through the crowd and the announce table. Afterward, the rest of the Establishment (Michael Stevens, Jason Dread, and Khan) ran in and beat Badger down further, Khan finishing with an Arabian Facebuster off the top rope onto a street sign.

Billed on the card as “Khan & Jason Dread vs. the Jhub & Rich "The Renegade" Rollins”. Khan pinned the Jhub with an Arabian Facebuster after Establishment members Toxic and Michael Stevens interfered on the floor; World Champion Jason Dread was Khan's partner, and Rich "The Renegade" Rollins was the Jhub's. Afterward, NBK, Badger Benandanti and Octavian ran in to help the Jhub and Rollins turn the tables on the whole Establishment.

Billed on the card as “Toad vs. Jeff Wylde”. GCW Commissioner Pete tried to help Jeff Wylde against Toad, but the interference misfired -- Toad ended up clobbering Pete by mistake -- and Wylde rolled Toad up with his feet on the ropes for the pin regardless.

Billed on the card as “TAK ("The Almighty Kippo") vs. the Tyrant”. In the Tyrant's GCW debut, he low-blowed TAK behind the referee's back and finished him with a powerbomb-facebuster combination for the pin.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW United States Championship: Twisted vs. Michael Stevens”. Unresolved. Toxic pulled the referee out during Twisted's Trash Compactor cover on champion Michael Stevens; Jason Dread and Khan then ran in and beat Twisted down, Dread finishing with a Tres Flores onto a chair and the No Moment (Twisted taps out to it, but no referee count or title change is described). No winner or title result is declared.

notes: Also on the card: “TAK ("The Almighty Kippo") vs. the Tyrant”. Unresolved. Toxic pulled the referee out during Twisted's Trash Compactor cover on champion Michael Stevens; Jason Dread and Khan then ran in and beat Twisted down, Dread finishing with a Tres Flores onto a chair and the No Moment (Twisted taps out to it, but no referee count or title change is described). No winner or title result is declared.

name: Meltdown 34

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Bridget & "The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. Katanya & Toxic”. US champion (not defended here) Toxic had already hit the Toxic Waste on Hanson with the referee distracted by Katanya and Bridget outside; Hanson then chaired Toxic with the title belt itself for the pin.

matches.stipulation: special guest referee Rich Rollins, special guest ring announcer Jason Dread
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Guest-Officiated Match: Badger Benandanti vs. The Jhub”. Referee Rollins twice stalled a legitimate Badger pin on the Jhub with transparent excuses; Badger ultimately won by referee stoppage, applying the BadgerClutch until the Jhub passed out rather than tapping. Post-match, Rollins and Dread jumped both losing-side men, but Badger and the Jhub turned it around, locking both attackers (BadgerClutch on Dread, Sharpshooter on Rollins) into simultaneous submissions -- setting up the NC-17 pairings (Dread/Badger, Rollins/the Jhub) rather than deciding this match, already over by then.

Billed on the card as “Mr. Danger & Octavian vs. President Steven Caldera & Tristain Mayhem”. Mayhem pinned champion Octavian (World Heavyweight Championship not at stake) with a Hammer On after Caldera hit Octavian with a low blow; an unidentified masked man had shoved Danger off the apron moments earlier, read by the commentary as a preview of Caldera's promised NC-17 partner reveal. A second brawl ran alongside the whole match (Badger and the Jhub ran in against a returning Jason Dread and Rich Rollins) without bearing on this match's own decided pin. Mayhem snatched Octavian's own title belt afterward and held it up, though no title change is recorded from this.
Billed on the card as “Jeff Wylde vs. Misdirection”. Misdirection won with a rollup after Twisted, ringside, distracted Wylde for just long enough.

notes: The fed's own booking record dates this card 9 October 2001; the card's own text dates it 15 November 2001, and the card settles the day. Both readings stand. Also on the card: “Jeff Wylde vs. Misdirection”. Misdirection won with a rollup after Twisted, ringside, distracted Wylde for just long enough.

name: Meltdown 35

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Hardy vs. Capo vs. Chris Jordan”. Mike Hardy flew in on Capo with a flying headscissors, then finished Chris Jordan with a Swanton Bomb for the pin -- a preview of the promotion's Cruiserweight scene. Afterward, "Awesome" Chris Edge and Lance Star ran in on Hardy, and Chameleon ran in to even the numbers.

Billed on the card as “Rich "The Renegade" Rollins, Jason Dread & Mr. Danger vs. The Jhub, Badger Benandanti & Steven Caldera”. Badger Benandanti locked the BadgerClutch on Rich Rollins, and Steven Caldera took out Mr. Danger's attempted save with a clothesline, forcing Rollins to submit. The Jhub and Jason Dread round out the sides.
Billed on the card as “Tristain Mayhem vs. Dan Rivero”. NBK shoved Dan Rivero off the turnbuckle mid-superplex block; Tristain Mayhem then finished him with the Hammer On (a running DDT) for the pin.

Billed on the card as “Hardcore Contest: Biggs vs. Agent Steel”. Biggs set Agent Steel up on a table and finished him with a DragonSteiner through it, earning a Hardcore title shot at NC-17 against Dimensioner.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Television Championship: Lance Star vs. NBK”. Dan Rivero pulled the referee out and belt-shotted champion NBK before he and Lance Star double-teamed him; the card's own text states NBK won by disqualification and retained.

Dan Rivero pulled the referee out and belt-shotted champion NBK before he and Lance Star double-teamed him; the card's own text states NBK won by disqualification and retained; “Tristain Mayhem vs. Dan Rivero”. NBK shoved Dan Rivero off the turnbuckle mid-superplex block; Tristain Mayhem then finished him with the Hammer On (a running DDT) for the pin.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Triple Threat Tag Match: Chris Jordan & Chris Edge vs. Capo & Lance Star vs. Chameleon & Michael Hardy”. Determines the two remaining Cruiserweight-title finalists and the four lumberjacks for bout 6, not itself a title match. Side 1 (Chris Jordan & Chris Edge) was eliminated first (Hardy pinned Edge after a Chameleon legdrop); side 2 (Capo, & Lance Star) was eliminated second (Chameleon pinned Star after Hardy's Swanton Bomb). The four losing-side wrestlers (Jordan, Edge, Capo, Star) become the lumberjacks for bout 6.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW United States Championship, Survival Match (steel cell): Luke Hanson vs. Toxic”. Toxic retained over Luke Hanson, "the Fueler", pinning him after a Falling Star off the top of the broken cell, with a decisive assist from Hanson's own manager Bridget, who chaired Hanson from behind mid-match.

Billed on the card as “Street Fight: Mr. Danger vs. President Steven Caldera”. President Steven Caldera beat Mr. Danger after three decoy masked men (dispatched by World Champion Octavian, appearing here only as an angle beat, not a side) turned out to be misdirection for a fourth masked man who hit Danger with a Cradle Tombstone and unmasked as John Reed, letting Caldera make the cover.

Billed on the card as “ACWF Three (no-disqualification parking-lot brawl): the Jhub vs. Rich Rollins”. The Jhub made Rich Rollins submit to the Sharpshooter, applied fifteen feet in the air on a raised forklift platform, after both men traded a top-of-the-semi superkick and a top-rope Anarchist Elbow into a truck bed below.

Billed on the card as “Number One Contendership to the GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Jason Dread vs. Badger Benandanti”. The card's own finish is a double pin: after a superplex, both men lay an arm across the other, and Mr. Danger (an angle beat, not a side -- he counted a fast pin for Dread on this same bout while the original referee simultaneously counted for Badger) and the original (unnamed) referee both count three at once; Joey Andrews's own ring announcement declares BOTH Jason Dread and Badger Benandanti the winners and co-Number One Contenders. No single winner is declared; the result is the card's own double pin.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-cruiserweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Cruiserweight Championship, Lumberjack Match: Michael Hardy vs. Chameleon”. Chameleon became the new GCW Cruiserweight Champion, pinning Michael "Hickenbottom" After the bell, Mike Hardy and Chameleon together cleared the lumberjacks with a double Arabian Facebuster through two tables, and Mike Hardy handed Chameleon the belt himself.

notes: Also on the card: “GCW Hardcore Championship: Dimensioner vs. Biggs”. Biggs retained the GCW Hardcore Championship over Dimensioner after ambushing him before the bell and sending him off the stage in a shopping cart. Toad then interfered, chairing Biggs and diving off the stage with a Toad Jam onto the pile; he is an angle beat, not a side -- the referee's count and the announcers' own read both settle Biggs as beating Dimensioner, with Toad's run-in changing nothing about who was pinned; “Lion's Den Match for a Judgment Call: Zippy vs. Gidget”. A comedic squash: Zippy and Gidget bring a television into the Lion's Den and watch cartoons instead of fighting; Gidget wins by default when a struggle over a soda can knocks Zippy out; “Jeff Wylde vs. Jonny Montano”. Jonny Montano pinned Jeff Wylde with a roundhouse kick he calls the Mexican Revolution, in Montano's pay-per-view debut; “GCW Television Championship: NBK vs. Dan Rivero”. NBK, Natural Born Killer beat Dan "The Main Event" Rivero with an inverted powerbomb he calls the 38 Special, to become the new GCW Television Champion; “GCW Cruiserweight Championship, Lumberjack Match: Michael Hardy vs. Chameleon”. Chameleon became the new GCW Cruiserweight Champion, pinning Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy with a floated-over pin off a reversed superplex, despite repeated interference from the four lumberjacks (Chris Jordan, Chris Edge, Capo, Lance Star -- the losing sides of bout 4). After the bell, Hardy and Chameleon together cleared the lumberjacks with a double Arabian Facebuster through two tables, and Hardy handed Chameleon the belt himself.

name: Meltdown 36

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti vs. Toxic”. Badger won by submission with the BadgerClutch, Toxic tapping despite Bridget's ringside distraction and a chair shot Toxic had landed moments earlier. Mr. Danger, Jason Dread and Octavian then ran in for a post-match beatdown of Badger and were themselves driven off by the Jhub, Toad and Luke Hanson, who publicly reformed System-X together to close the show; none of this changed the already-decided submission result. Rich Rollins was reported unable to travel; not a competitor tonight.

A brutal squash establishing a legitimate-angle injury: Wylde used brass knuckles, his own second Roadblock's interference, and finally a chair-assisted knee drop through a table to finish Mike Hardy, who was ruled out with bruised ribs and a mild concussion, expected back in a week. A returning Chameleon repeatedly tried to even the odds against Roadblock but could not prevent the finish.

Billed on the card as “The Grim Reaper vs. Johnny Montano”. An upset: Montano won with a top-rope elbow drop after a facebuster; the Reaper no-sold the loss, walking out unfazed as if the result didn't matter to him.

name: Meltdown 37

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti vs. Tristain Mayhem”. Octavian chaired Mayhem from behind just as Mayhem set up a Hammer On on Badger, and the referee called for the bell before either man could be pinned; no winner is announced. Jason Dread then ran in to chair Badger but Mayhem ducked and Dread accidentally hit Octavian, and Badger chaired Dread in turn -- all after the match had already been called off. This confirmed the Christmas Chaos fatal fourway for the World Heavyweight Championship: Octavian (c) vs. Jason Dread vs. Badger Benandanti vs. Tristain Mayhem.

Billed on the card as “Jason Dread, Toxic & Octavian vs. Toad, "The Fueler" Luke Hanson & The Jhub”. System-X's reunion match. The Jhub hit a Downward Spiral on champion Octavian while not the legal man, and Toad (having just tagged in) followed with a top-rope Toad Jam for the pin -- the broadcast itself calls the finish less than clean, though the win is recorded as System-X's. Mr. Danger ran in with a chair but was cut off by a returning John Reed before he could affect the match. World Heavyweight Championship not at stake.
Billed on the card as “The Grim Reaper vs. Capo”. Capo dominated and won with a schoolboy rollup.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Tag Team Championship: Chameleon & Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy vs. Twisted & Misdirection”. Challengers Chameleon and Mike Hardy won new championships when Chameleon reversed a Twisted whip into his finisher, ‘the Strike’ (a reverse DDT/DVD), for the pin. Post-match, Jeff Wylde ran in and attacked the injured Mike Hardy further before Chameleon beat him off with a lead pipe.

Mike Hardy ran in and speared champion Toxic for no stated reason, and the referee called the match off; no winner is announced. A four-way brawl followed (Hardy vs. the Jhub, Toad vs. Toxic) before officials separated everyone, none of it resolving the title match itself.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Toad vs. Octavian”. IN-RING RESULT: Toad won the title clean, pinning Octavian after Jason Dread's chair swing (meant for Toad) accidentally struck champion Octavian instead. Danger then overturned the decision by video review minutes later, ruling Dread's interference (against his own ally Octavian) a disqualification in Octavian's favor and restoring the World title to him on the spot -- an administrative reversal, not a second match, following the same pattern as the Women's title reversal on Meltdown 33. Toad's own Hardcore championship was never in jeopardy either way, since Toad was the one who won the pinfall, not the one pinned.

Billed on the card as “Street Fight: John Reed vs. Mr. Danger”. John Reed had Mr. Danger beaten (a fire extinguisher blast had also knocked out the referee), but Dan Rivero ran in, hit a top-rope Rivero Elbow on John Reed, and physically manipulated the unconscious referee's hand to count Mr. Danger's pin.

Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti & Tristain Mayhem vs. Jason & Pete”. A comedic squash: Badger pinned Pete with a moonsault and Tristain Mayhem pinned Jason with a top-rope powerbomb (Hammer On DDT) simultaneously, the referee counting both down together. Afterward, in a meaningless post-bell bit, a groggy Jason rolled onto the already-pinned Pete and self-declared a win with his own slow count; this has no bearing on the match, already decided.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Tag Team Championship: Capo & Big Skails vs. Chameleon & Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy”. Champions Hardy and Chameleon retained; Hardy pinned Skails with a Swanton Bomb despite injured ribs throughout. Post-match, Skails chaired his own brother Capo, apparently resenting the loss; no bearing on the already-decided title match. Big Skails has none.

Billed on the card as “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. Tristain Mayhem”. Mayhem hit a Hammer On on Hanson, but Jason Dread (scouting ringside ahead of their own Christmas Chaos fatal fourway) held the referee, voiding the cover; a mass brawl followed -- Mayhem crossbodied Dread, but a man in the crowd (revealed as Octavian) threw a fireball that burned Mayhem's face, and Octavian locked on a Roman Rapper before Dread accidentally hit him and Badger Benandanti made Dread tap to a BadgerClutch. No bell ever closes the match itself, and no winner is announced.

Billed on the card as “Non-Title Match: Natural Born Killer vs. The Jhub”. Champion (TV title, not defended) NBK had the Jhub in a Sharpshooter when Toxic ran in and hit the Jhub with the US title belt and a Toxic Waste; the referee called for the bell, ruling the Jhub the winner by disqualification. A further brawl followed (the Jhub hit NBK with a Downward Spiral; Mike Hardy belted the Jhub; Toad chaired and Toad-Jammed Hardy) with no bearing on the already-decided DQ.
Billed on the card as “Badger Benandanti vs. Johnny Montano”. Badger won by submission with the BadgerClutch.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship, ambush sequence: Rick Diamond vs. Toad vs. Phyl vs. Toad”. Three referee-counted falls in rapid succession backstage: Rick Diamond (the character formerly billed Dimensioner) blindsided champion Toad with a chair and pinned him, becoming champion; Phyl immediately rolled Diamond up for the pin and the title; Toad then chaired both men and pinned Phyl, regaining the title he had lost moments before. The card records all three changes and no single winner, since the title passed hands twice within the one segment.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hardcore
matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW Hardcore Championship: Toad vs. Michael "Hickenbottom" Hardy”. Hardy ambushed champion Toad before any formal start, battering him with a brick and an equipment case through the backstage area to a loading dock; both men fell roughly ten feet off the dock together, and a referee who had followed them counted Toad's pin on top. Hardy was taken to a hospital, his third serious injury angle in under two months.

Billed on the card as “"The Fueler" Luke Hanson vs. Jason Dread”. Hanson won with a chair shot and pin after World Champion Tristain Mayhem's presence at ringside distracted Dread at the decisive moment; Mayhem never physically entered the match.

Billed on the card as “Non-Title Match: Toxic vs. Chameleon”. No finish: Octavian ran in, chaired both a recovering Chameleon and an intervening Mike Hardy, then left with Toxic without explanation; no bell or pinfall closes the match, and no winner is announced.
Billed on the card as “Rampage Tournament Qualifier: Erick Caine vs. Hades”. Caine's debut; he won and advanced in the tournament with a bridged German suplex.
Billed on the card as “Bruce "The Tradition" Moore vs. The Evangelist”. Moore's debut, won with a superkick.

Billed on the card as “Big Skails vs. Capo”. An upset: Skails's associates 3-Pak and Icebabe repeatedly interfered (a shoe shot, a chair shot, a distraction) against Capo, Skails's own brother, letting Skails pin him.

Billed on the card as “Rampage Tournament Qualifier: Michael "Spitfire" Stevens vs. John Reed”. Michael Stevens's debut. Jason O'Neil (billed ‘The Dark Messiah’) ran in, powerbombed John Reed on the floor, then hit him with a Nightmare Driver onto exposed concrete, before forcing the previously-knocked-out referee to count Michael Stevens's pin on the unconscious John Reed.

Double Cool (Tristain Mayhem and Jennifer Krug) became the NEW GCW Tag Team Champions, pinning Toxic (a member of the third side, not the outgoing champions) after Mayhem's DDT, amid heavy outside interference: President Steven Caldera and John Reed ran in on Octavian; the Lunatic handcuffed champion Mike Hardy to the ring post and carried off his partner Chameleon; and Katanya chair-shotted Octavian, costing the outgoing champions (Hardy/Chameleon) and Toxic/Octavian the fall. matches.note: Billed on the card as “GCW World Heavyweight Championship: Badger Benandanti vs. Jason Dread”. No contest. With Dread's Establishment stablemates all taken out earlier in the show (Khan by the Jhub, Steven Caldera by Octavian, Stevens by NBK, Toxic by Rollins), champion Jason Dread and challenger Badger Benandanti wrestled one-on-one until debuting Low pulled the referee out during Badger's cover off a BadgerBuster, entered the ring, and shoved both men out without a fall. No winner is announced. Four officials named only by surname (Giles, St. Clair, Salazar and Shin) pulled Uropa and Sheena away.

The commentary names every Syphen move (the Syphen Knifin', SYPHilis, SYPHocation, the SYPHening, Prioritization, InSYPHicient and the DiSYPHEr). A replay of the top-rope spear is shown from two angles.

Hardy was busted open, appeared unconscious and was checked on by officials (St. Clair, Salazar and Giles are named by surname), a second referee and the trainers; he got up under his own power. Two replays are shown (the top-rope facebuster and the barricade).

It is fought in the backstage area of the Arrowhead Pond (a food table, a coffee pot, hockey sticks and pucks, a net and a shelf of equipment), with a referee following the men; Toad is first seen watching Mike Hardy on a monitor.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.finish: The Tyrant hit the Tyrant Plant on The Evangelist and referee Briggs counted the three, making The Tyrant the new Television Champion.
matches.note: No heading is printed; Bryan announces it as "the Fatal Fourway for the Television title" and the ring announcer as a "Fatal Fourway Match up". Played under tag rules: any man in the ring could tag any other, as Yale explains. Demented, the champion, was not pinned: The Tyrant won by pinning The Evangelist. Earlier, Demented hit the Fatality on Knight and covered, and The Tyrant pulled the referee out of the ring at two to save the fall; a replay of The Tyrant slamming Demented to the floor is shown. The announcer calls The Tyrant "the NEW GCW TELEVISION CHAMPION". A recap of the build (Demented winning the number-one-contender rumble and then the title from The Evangelist at Sub Zero) runs before the match.

matches.note: Announced in the ring as "a ten man elimination match for the GCW World Heavyweight Championship": the Establishment against the Resistance, five against five, with Low as special guest referee. Rollins and Toxic, both eliminated, brawled up the ramp. Low missed a tag from the Resistance while talking to Michael Stevens, watched the stage instead of the ring during a cover, eliminated Octavian with the fastest three count of the night, and ended the match with Badger's foot on the rope, so the commentators accuse him of favouring the Establishment. Luke Hanson, not an entrant, ran in from the crowd to help the Establishment, and Toxic and Khan, already eliminated, took part in later falls. Caldera pulled Dread from the ring after the bell, and the page ends on Badger's fury and the Road to Warpath.

notes: The fed's own Television Title history dates a title change to Dread Reckoning on 17 March 2002, and its booking record held no card for it; this is that show. The page prints no date, but it shows The Tyrant win the Television Title in a Fatal Fourway, as the title history says, and it promises the one-year-anniversary Meltdown for "this Thursday" (Meltdown 51 is dated Thursday, 21 March 2002). The page names the venue as the Arrowhead Pond and gives a crowd of 17,000.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-tag-team

The card's own text ends there ("LeStatt is the only conscious one in the ring! What's going to happen now?") and cuts to the next segment with no finish given. eliminations.note: Eliminated by the whole field at once, in unison, seconds after the bell; the text names no single eliminator.
Dan Black bulldozes in and launches Patrick Vander over the top after Phil Atken and Daria Ngozi had already worn him down.
Accidental: Jake Reed, rushing to help McKail skin-the-cat back into the ring, catches him head-first in the midsection and knocks him out to the floor.
Self-elimination: appalled at having just cost McKail the match, Reed climbs out of the ring under his own power to chase after him.
Keegan O'Conner and Dan Black combine, Black's freight-train shoulder finishing the job Atken and Daria Ngozi had started on him earlier.

Daria Ngozi's Capoeira kick to the back of O'Conner's head buckles his support arm; Dan Black shoves his legs the rest of the way over.

matches.note: Billed as "Singles Match - One Fall"; Almasy's first bout in GCW and the show's main event, a non-title match because Borealis (the United States Champion) refused to put the belt up. The wager, made earlier in the night: if Almasy won, Rollins signs for a FallOut match with him; if he lost, he leaves GCW that night. The Cactuar Crossface is his signature hold, the Jecht Shot a spinning roundhouse kick and the Lunatic Pandora a moonsault leg drop. Afterwards Rollins appeared on the stage and clapped slowly, and the two stared at each other as the show ended.

eliminations.note: Cade Carson thrown out; Axel Action flips his feet off the mat as Carson tries to dump Dan Black, and Carson himself goes over instead.
Tyson DeBough, perched on the apron, is hurricanrana'd off it by Vivica J. Valentine and lands in Shaman's arms outside.
Double elimination: Kris Michaels scooped up James Mercier and ran him over the top rope, and both men hit the floor together.
Double elimination: Kris Michaels carried James Mercier over the top rope and both men hit the floor together.
Lori Equinox grabs SurReal from behind to lift him out, but SurReal hooks his legs under Equinox's arms and flips over, tossing Equinox out instead.
Digital Mortality (armed with a steel chair the instant he enters at #22) blindsides Bishop Steele with a chair shot that sends him over the top.
Joe Milone, moments after entering at #23, is scooped up by Shaman and flung over the top rope -- lasted eight seconds by the broadcast's own count.
Bryan Mayhem (entering at #25) hoists 300-pound Jorge Samuelsson and drops him over the top rope with an Oblivion Bomb.

LeStatt Knight throws Clyde Fox out by his legs; Fox hooks Knight's neck with a flying headscissor on the way out and drags the three-time champion to the floor with him -- Knight is gone, Fox survives on the apron. Knight lasted well under two minutes from his #27 entrance.
Markus Stone, leaping the guardrail from the crowd unannounced, pulled Tessa Windsor over the top rope by the hair from behind and fled.
Digital Mortality sneaks in from behind and flips Lantlas Anduril's legs off the mat and over the top rope.

Shaman launches Cheap Labor at Bryan Mayhem as a projectile; Mayhem catches Labor but loses his own balance and flips out of the ring. The broadcast credits Labor with the elimination ('Labor will get credit for the elimination there') while naming Shaman's strength as what actually did it.
Cheap Labor, having snuck back in, is caught by Dan Black and thrown overhead into the floor with a belly-to-belly suplex.

Zacharia Taylor pulls the top rope down as Aaron Nothings charges in with a flying dropkick; Nothings sails over the lowered rope, bounces off CJ Woods's body and lands on the floor. Nothings lasted the entire match from the #1 draw.
CJ Woods, having just put Shaman on the back foot, is grabbed by the throat and slung violently over the top rope, landing hard on the floor.

Dan Black grabs Axel Action from behind, but Axel dives out of the ring holding the top rope, carrying a shocked Black with him -- Axel skins the cat back to his feet inside the ring while Black drops to the floor.

Clyde Fox springs off Axel Action's back into a body block on Shaman, driving both men over the top rope together; Fox hangs on the ropes, Shaman drops to the floor. Shaman's own run is the match's longest single dominant stretch -- five eliminations of his own, entering at #3, out a shade under seventy minutes in.
Digital Mortality counters a turnbuckle suplex attempt with a floatover powerbomb off the top, putting Axel Action on the floor. Axel entered at #2 and very nearly went the distance.
Zacharia Taylor bites Digital Mortality's fingers off the top rope he is clinging to after being knocked off the apron, dropping him to the floor beside Axel Action.
Clyde Fox low-bridged the top rope as Zacharia Taylor charged, sending Taylor out of the ring to land hard on his head; Valentine, Terror and Fox remained.

M3 dives off the top rope with a twisting plancha onto SurReal, who is holding Clyde Fox up for a jackhammer; all three fly out through the ropes, and SurReal is the one who hits the floor (Fox and M3 both land on the apron).

Vivica J. Valentine catches Clyde Fox's cross-body attempt, holds her balance, then wrenches him over the ropes and throws him to the floor -- the broadcast calls her the winner in the instant before Terror's return swerve.

Jay Terror -- who went to the floor earlier brawling with Valentine at the announce table and simply never re-entered, unnoticed and never himself eliminated (he was never thrown over the top rope) -- clotheslines a celebrating Valentine over the top rope an instant after she eliminates Fox, and is awarded the match. Winner: Jay Terror (#30).

eliminations.note: A mass pin before the falls-count threshold was reached: T.A. Giles, Tempest, AXEL Action, Cheap Labor, Triumph Frost, Slash, The Magnificent Messiah and Kid Cool all piled onto Roxx after his own missed high spot; Clyde Fox counted the fall.
AXEL Action covers Richter at the bottom of the arena stairs; referee Cameron Wrigley counts.
Bryan Mayhem chokeslams Fujita (Lucifer's Grip) onto the hood of a car in the parking lot; referee Hal Jenkins counts.
PAZUZU pins Cheap Labor in the ring; GBJ himself makes the count.
PAZUZU's Full Nelson Ham Sandwich (a full-nelson slam); GBJ counts.

Shaman Death Valley Drivered his own tag partner in the parking lot after Tim Shipley's car crashed into the one Shaman and Bryan Mayhem were fighting on; referee Hal Jenkins counted. This count set the field at sixteen and began the Rampage seeding.
Seed 16. PAZUZU's Lawsuit (Samoan-drop-style slam) onto a chair; referee Timothy Vale counts.
Seed 15. Rasa's Flying Triangle Choke; Slash taps.
Seed 14. Already-eliminated Slash lays the (also-just-eliminated) Magnificent Messiah on top of Equinox after a chair barrage; Timothy Vale counts the fall as Messiah's.
Seed 13. The Magnificent Messiah scoop-slams and leg-drops Kid Cool for the pin, with an assist (not the fall) from Tempest.
Seed 12. Bryan Mayhem, posing as a cab driver in the parking lot, chokeslams Atken (Lucifer's Grip) on the pavement; referee Hal Jenkins counts.
Seed 11. Rasa's arm-triangle submission; Johnson taps.
Seed 10. PAZUZU's Lawsuit onto a chair; Timothy Vale counts.
Seed 9. PAZUZU pins Messiah, still down from a suicide-dive chair shot; Timothy Vale counts.
Seed 8. Backstage: Tim Shipley baits AXEL Action into a room, Cheap Labor breaks a cement block over his head from behind the door, and Shipley pins him; both David Fellows and Clyde Fox count.
Seed 7. Rasa's roundhouse-kick-into-Tiger-Crush-triangle-choke; Frost taps.
Seed 6. Tempest's running schoolboy roll-up; Josh Briggs counts.
Seed 5. Rasa needlessly hooks a leg on the already-fallen Spencer (set up by Triumph Frost's own earlier offense) and pins him.
Seed 4. Tim Shipley dives off the stage onto PAZUZU, landing on top of him; GBJ counts.
Rasa's Tiger Crush off a ladder set up earlier in the match (seed 3, by the later Rampage bracket cards); Garbage Bag Johnny counted.
Seed 2. Tim Shipley's Eternal Hope (a springboard neckbreaker) onto a steel chair; GBJ counts for the match's final fall.

eliminations.note: Clyde Fox clotheslines Brian Fisher over the top rope (~15 minutes into the match).
Chris Bagwell launches Aaron Fujita over the top rope moments after Fujita's entrance.
Bryan Mayhem powerbombs Rikki Roxx on the stage on his entrance, then simply flips him off his shoulder and over the top rope in the ring.
Bryan Mayhem catches La Sombra out of a corkscrew cross body attempt and fallaway-slams him out of the ring.
Johnny Borealis, ziplining into the ring, catches Phil Atken with a missile dropkick.
Johnny Borealis springboard-dropkicks Jimmy Thunder off the apron and into the guardrail, after Bryan Mayhem had already forearmed him down.
Self-elimination: Chris Storm hops over the top rope of his own accord immediately after piledriving Johnny Borealis through a steel chair; never attacked or eliminated by anyone.
Andy Murray shoves a battered Scott Stevens over the top rope after landing dozens of unanswered punches on him.
Chris Bagwell counters a Dan Black elimination attempt, wrapping his legs around Black's head and tossing him to the floor.
Johnny Borealis clotheslines Dynasty, who had just skinned the cat back onto the apron after a Tempest dropkick.
Shaman shot-puts AXEL Action clear of the ring and onto the entrance ramp's metal grating.
Chris Bagwell baited Tyson DeBough and Brian Fisher (already eliminated, and back in the ring illegally) into a tandem lariat, then pulled the top rope down and sent both flying out.
Chris Bagwell clotheslines the Magnificent Messiah over the top rope on his entrance.
Aimz casually flips Rediker over the top rope shortly after his own entrance.
Shaman rams a steel ladder into Dorn Tracer's spine, driving him over the top rope.
Dominic Wall clotheslines Alexander Redding over the top rope moments after Wall's own entrance.
Johnny Borealis springboard-suplexes and kicks El Moreno out after Chris Bagwell had already worn him down.
Triumph Frost guerilla-presses Aimz and hurls her out of the ring, landing her near the announce table.
Rasa (pre-reveal) hooks the top rope with an arm and a leg while grappling with Bryan Mayhem and drags him out with her own body weight, staying in herself by curling her legs clear of the floor.
Andy Murray clotheslines Clyde Fox over the top rope after Fox turns his back to taunt the crowd.
Johnny Borealis and Chris Bagwell eliminated each other, both toppling to the floor together after a prolonged tug-of-war over the top rope.
Went out together with Chris Bagwell after the tug-of-war over the top rope.
Rasa (pre-reveal), in a last-ditch escape from a Tempest/Valentine double elimination attempt, wraps both arms around Tempest's head and drags her out instead of herself.

Referee Josh Briggs rules Vivica J. Valentine eliminated when her hair (not her body) brushes the floor mats while she escapes a Karina Wolfenden throw onto the apron -- a technicality, argued furiously at the time.
Triumph Frost flips both his and Karina Wolfenden's ankles out from under them as she has him dangling over the top rope; Wolfenden has no way to save herself and crashes to the floor.
Andy Murray catches Triumph Frost out of a top-rope cross body and powers him out of the ring for the win.

eliminations.note: Backbody dropped over the top rope by Phillip Kennedy moments after Kennedy entered.
A cannon stunt entrance backfired: he was launched over the ropes into the crowd guardrail before he ever wrestled a contested spot; no one eliminated him.
Caught by the throat on Rasa's own entry and flung over the top rope like a ragdoll.
Powerbombed out of the ring by Rasa after landing body shots to no visible effect.
Kicked, then lariat'd over the top rope by Rasa almost immediately on entry.
Flung out by her hair by Desade almost immediately on entry, moments after a springboard dropkick of her own on Kasidy Drake.
Climbed back out of the ring unprompted after one look at Rasa and left with his entourage without ever wrestling a contested spot; no one eliminated him.
Sneaking up on Rasa from behind, Drake was spotted, grabbed by the trunks and thrown over the top rope by Kennedy.
Backpedalled from Rasa in vain; caught by the throat, lifted and hurled out of the ring.
Sneaking up on Vivica J. Valentine from behind, Searle was up-ended by a charging Frankie Valleta.
Eliminated by Valentine moments after entering, while trying to hoist Desade over (“Fujita's gone just like that!”).
Revealed as the surprise twenty-fifth entrant, he announced that his GCW contract had lapsed and jumped over the top rope unprompted, quitting on air; no one laid a hand on him.
Two running shoulderblocks from Frankie Valleta sent Shaman over the top rope in the match's final stretch.
Backdropped high into the air by Desade after a missile dropkick on Frankie Valleta; landed hard on the floor.

Blindsided by Terrence Kingsley, who used her own forward momentum (she was charging at Desade) to dump her out of the ring; Valentine tried to force her way back in and was held off by a wall of officials.
Desade's Spider's Kiss sent her flying backwards over the top rope.
Deflected by Alexander Redding into Sexton Hardon's waiting arms, who flipped her over the top rope.
A final extended kick from Desade sent him to the outside after she had already torn into him at length.
Hardon and Kennedy were too locked up fighting each other to see Rasa coming; Rasa clotheslined both over the top rope together.
Clotheslined over the top rope by Rasa together with Sexton Hardon.
Desade and Brad Jackson each grabbed a leg and flipped Rasa out of the ring together, the two of them nearly spent doing it (“Rasa's gone! Good lord, they did it!”).

Final elimination: Jackson pulled the top rope down as an exhausted Desade leapt at him with a flying forearm; she sailed over the ropes and landed on the floor without Jackson going over himself. Brad Jackson, last man standing, won the GCW World Heavyweight Championship match at NC-17.
