matches.finish: Borealis tilted Pearce into the Hecatomb (a tilt-a-whirl piledriver) and covered him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jonathan Borealis vs. Connor Pearce”. Kyle Niker, still sore from his loss to El Rayo Azul II, came out with Pearce, helped him to his feet at ringside during the bout and checked on him afterwards. Billed with the spelling “Connor Pearce”.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.finish: With Toxic on the stage holding up the Twistodium bottle he had taken from Twizzy's corner, Knight turned Twizzy around, hit the Knight Fall and covered him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “United States Title Match – LeStatt Knight vs. Twizzy”. Afterwards Knight, handed his belt, stared into the distance and ignored the referee raising his hand.

matches.finish: Hardy hit a shooting star press from a twenty-foot ladder onto The Dark Messiah in the wrecked ring and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Hardy vs. The Dark Messiah”. The ring collapsed under Hardy's moonsault from the ladder and The Dark Messiah kicked out twice before the shooting star press; he was taken out on a stretcher, and the result line reads “Winner: Mike Hardy”.

matches.finish: Dread put Mr. Danger in the No Moment and Danger tapped out.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jason Dread vs. Alex Blaq vs. Luke Hanson vs. Mr. Danger vs. Octavian”. A five-man battle royal with the World Heavyweight Champion as the lone target of the Praetorian Guard. The card does not bill Blaq's Hardcore Title or Dread's World Title as on the line.

notes: Numbered from the weekly run: WorldWide 11 is dated 4 May 2005 and WorldWide 16 is dated 9 June 2005 by the fed's own booking, and the pages dated 5-11-05, 5-19-05, 5-26-05 and 6-2-05 are the four editions between them. Also on the card: A side of this bout, El Rayo Azul II, is not yet tied to a character record, so the bout is filed without sides. Billed as “El Rayo Azul vs. Kyle Niker”; the result line reads “Winner: El Rayo Azul II”. Connor Pearce watched from ringside; referee Fellows counted.

name: WorldWide 14

date.source: the page's own dating (5-26-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Twizzy hit Toxic with the Pill Popper and The Jhub hit Luke Hanson with the Downward Spiral, each covered his man, and the two three counts fell in unison.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Toxic vs. Luke Hanson”. The Jhub and Twizzy came out first in black-and-white striped shirts and acted as the bout's officials (Twizzy called for the bell; The Jhub separated the two men), then turned on both men and pinned them in unison; the card ends “Winners: The Jhub and Twizzy”.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.finish: Knight, bloodied by a Spike DDT, climbed after Borealis on the top rope and hit a top-rope Knight Fall, draping an arm over him for the three count.
matches.note: No heading is printed; the match is announced in Borealis's own promo and the text calls it a United States Title match. Knight, the champion, retained.

matches.finish: Hardy hit a shooting star press on both members of Allied Chaos, pushed Connor Pearce off and covered Kyle Niker for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Hardy vs. Allied Chaos”. Hardy took on both members of Allied Chaos at once.

matches.finish: As Octavian raised his Imperial Roman belt over Trey, Jason Dread snatched it away, and Trey sprang off the ropes with both feet into Octavian's chest and pinned him.
matches.note: No heading is printed; the bout is the show's main event, set up in Octavian's own promo, in which he said he would give Trey a preview of Warpath. Jordan White was at ringside with Trey; Trey, the Hardcore Champion, was handed his Hardcore Title belt after the win.

notes: Numbered from the weekly run (see WorldWide 12). The card calls itself the final WorldWide before Warpath, with Warpath in Houston on the Sunday.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “TV Title Battle Royal”. Entrants came in on the buzzer: Hardcastle and Marshall, then Kyle Niker, Erik VanLorne, Dimensioner, Borealis, Eva VanLorne, Connor Pearce, Ryan Stephens and Capo. Capo came out wearing the Television Title belt; Borealis took it off him and dropped it out of the ring. Marshall, already eliminated, returned with the belt and hit Stephens, and officials took the belt from him. Erik VanLorne is not yet tied to a character record and is named in the eliminations only.

matches.finish: Dimensioner hit the End of Reality chokeslam over his knee and covered Blaq for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Dimensioner vs. Alex Blaq”. Dimensioner entered for the second time that night after his early exit in the battle royal.

matches.finish: Rollins climbed to the top rope and hit the Anarchist Elbow on The Jhub and covered him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “The Jhub vs. Rich “The Renegade” Rollins”. Rollins's first GCW match in nearly four years. Under the wager he made with Hardy earlier in the night, a win lets him set the stipulation for Dangerous Games.

notes: Numbered from the weekly run (see WorldWide 12). The page is dated 6-2-05, the day the fed's own Television Title history dates the title to Johnathan Borealis (2 June 2005), and the card shows him winning it.

name: WorldWide 17

date.source: the page's own dating (6-16-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Johnson, kneeling and played possum, rolled the charging Twizzy into a small package and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Twizzy vs. Shawn Johnson”. Johnson, in his singles debut, kicked out of the Pill Popper, broke Twizzy's sharpshooter by clinging to the referee, and landed six fisherman suplexes; afterwards Twizzy lost his temper at ringside, accosted The Jhub at the announce table over his missing pills and staggered out.

matches.finish: With no referee in the ring, Rich Rollins lay down in the centre of the ring and Capo covered him; the crowd counted three, and the result line reads "Winner via pinfall: Capo".
matches.note: Billed as Mike Hardy vs. Capo; Hardy did not come out and Rollins came to the ring instead and gave Capo the unofficial pin as a mockery. Rollins then planted Capo with a Waterfall and climbed to the top rope; a fan in a Tsunami Oni mask jumped the rail, shoved him off, and was unmasked as Mike Hardy, who gave Capo a second Waterfall, said he had baited Rollins, and made their Dangerous Games Iron Man match a no-disqualification match, which Rollins accepted.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-tag-team
matches.finish: Erik and Eva VanLorne rushed the ring from behind and beat Dimensioner and Marshall down before the bell could start the match, and the referee declared it a No Contest.
matches.note: Billed as "Tag Team Title Match", EVL (Eva and Erik VanLorne, the champions; Erik is not yet tied to a character record) against Dimensioner and Bryan Marshall. Jordan White came out at the top of the stage as EVL's music played, and Erik and Eva attacked from behind; the champions kept the titles. After the bell Dimensioner lost his temper and slammed his own partner, Marshall, who was stretchered out.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.finish: After Borealis shook off referee David Fellows's hand, Fellows called for the bell and threw the match out, giving the win by disqualification to Hardcastle.
matches.note: Billed as "Television Title Match - One Fall"; Borealis (the champion) came out with a long promo in which he offered to defend the title at Dangerous Games against any two opponents. The page gives the win to Hardcastle by disqualification and names no new champion, so the title is recorded as not changing hands.

matches.finish: Stevens rolled Dread up in a school boy roll-up, yanking his tights for leverage, after Dread reversed his powerbomb, and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jason Dread & Trey Tremendous vs. LeStatt Knight & Michael Stevens”. Dread brought his World Title and Trey his United States and Hardcore Titles to the ring, but none was on the line. Knight tagged Stevens in and out of the bout to avoid Dread. After the bell Trey and Knight brawled until security separated them and Dread missed a shooting star press to the floor; the broadcast went off the air, and a closing note says the rest was fan footage kept by Caldera.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #17, and it follows WorldWide 16 (9 June 2005) in the weekly run. It is dated 6-16-05. Joey Andrews announces the ring entrances.

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Gauntlet Match for #30”. A gauntlet in which Borealis, the Television Champion, faced Hardcastle, Capo, Dimensioner and Luke Hanson in turn; the winner enters the Dangerous Games battle royal at number thirty. The belt was not on the line. Referees Josh Briggs, Tim Vale and Hal Jenkins worked it. Low, who was not announced as an opponent, pinned the exhausted champion and was named "the #30 Entrant".

matches.finish: A blackout let Jason Dread swap into the Disco Duck suit; as Knight went for a second Knight Fall Dread cobra-clutched him and bulldogged him, and the referee ended the match as a No Contest.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Disco Duck”. Knight, who had accepted the duck's challenge at Jacobs's interview, hit the Knight Fall and the count reached two when the lights went out for five or six seconds. Dread, in the suit, beat Knight until security separated them, and told him Dangerous Games was his game.

matches.finish: With Dread screaming in Stevens's cloverleaf, LeStatt Knight came through the crowd with a steel chair, knocked Stevens out cold with it and shattered the chair over Dread's head, and the match was declared a No Contest.
matches.note: Billed "Non-Title Match - One Fall"; Dread, the World Champion, put no title on the line. Trey Tremendous, the United States Champion, came out as Knight left the ring.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #18; it is dated 6-27-05 and is billed as the last WorldWide before Dangerous Games. Joey Andrews announces the entrances.

name: WorldWide 21

date.source: the page's own dating (8-18-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Meatshield Trainwrecker hit Dimensioner in the head with a bag of dice, lifted him, and The Rogue Paladin jumped up to complete the Guild's team finisher; referee Timothy Vale counted the three.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “The Guild vs. Dimensioner & X”. The Guild's debut; billed as "Tag Team Match - One Fall" with Timothy Vale named as referee in the page's own heading. Dimensioner and X, opponents on WorldWide 20, teamed badly: Dimensioner choked The Rogue Paladin while Vale warned him, X slapped him for the tag, and Dimensioner chokeslammed The Rogue Paladin. Vale caught that The Rogue Paladin had tagged Trainwrecker before Dimensioner's first cover, then The Guild won with the d20 finisher.

matches.finish: As Savige set Hardy up for a stalling vertical suplex and went for the cover, The Marauder broke the count with an elbow drop from the top rope and the referee called for the bell; the ring announcement reads "The Winner: Mike Savige via DQ".
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Savige vs. Mike Hardy”. Savige's first GCW match (his own promo on the next WorldWide says he had had only one). The page calls the bout thrown out because of The Marauder's run-in, then gives the decision to Savige by disqualification. After the bell The Marauder and Savige traded blows, and The Marauder took a wireless microphone from the announce table and said he had no match that week.

matches.finish: Octavian turned Twizzy into the Roman Rapper and Twizzy tapped; Joey Andrews announced Octavian the winner.
matches.note: Billed as "Octavian vs. Twisted" (the page calls him Twizzy in the narration); Octavian's first match back. Twizzy took the early lead with a short-arm clothesline, a double axe handle and a Rebel Yell to the ears, but Octavian answered with a thumb to the eye, a pump handle slam and three snap suplexes.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.finish: With Mayhem holding Rollins in a figure-four, X ran in and superkicked Mayhem, Trey Tremendous pulled the referee out of the ring, Borealis handed Mayhem a steel chair and Mayhem hit Rollins's legs with it until the referee called the bell; the announcement is cut off after "via disqualification, and STILL your GCW Television Champion".
matches.note: Billed as "Singles Match - One Fall"; Bryan Mayhem was the challenger and the Television Title was on the line. The ring announcer's line is drowned out by the crowd, so the page never names the winner; "STILL your GCW Television Champion" is Rollins, who kept the title. The page implies Mayhem was the one disqualified for the chair shots ("He may have cost himself this match"); he grinned as he took the chair and looked shocked when the bell rang. Afterwards Trey set the dented chair over Rollins and sat on it with the support bar across his throat before Trey and Borealis left.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #21; it is dated 8-18-05, follows WorldWide 20 (10 August 2005) and is billed two weeks before Annihilation, which the fed's title history dates 28 August 2005. Joey Andrews announces the entrances. Also on the card: Billed as "Michael Stevens vs. Raziel"; Knight had chosen the opponent, RaZiel (not yet tied to a character record), and told Stevens that Sheena would pay if he lost. Referee Josh Briggs checked the choke hold RaZiel put on Stevens. The screen showed Alex Morgan (not yet tied to a character record) attacking a man who looked like Knight; the man pulled off a black wig, maced RaZiel when he came to check on him, and Morgan shut RaZiel in a car trunk (Pete guesses the wigged man is Sheena's brother Lance, but is not sure). Stevens then told Knight that he now held someone of Knight's. The page closes on an angry voice screaming behind Knight's boarded-up dressing-room door.

name: WorldWide 22

date.source: the page's own dating (8-25-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: As Dimensioner covered Capo after a sit-down powerbomb and the referee counted "TW-", The Fraud Squad (Frederick Fraud and Finean) came out with whistles, Finean dropped Dimensioner with an inverted backbreaker, and the bell rang; Joey Andrews announced Dimensioner the winner by disqualification.
matches.note: Billed as "Capo vs. Dimensioner"; the crowd chanted against Capo, "our inaugural Television Champion". Capo missed a suicide plancha, was thrown into the ring post fifteen times and took a seven-foot sit-down powerbomb before the count was broken up. The Fraud Squad (not yet tied to character records) then blew whistles in the ring and announced themselves.

matches.finish: X hopped the guardrail onto the apron and drew Mayhem's eye, then ran off; Mayhem turned into a kick to the gut and the Machinehead, and Savige covered for the three.
matches.note: Billed as "Singles Match - One Fall". After the bell The Marauder came over the barricade with a steel chair and stopped at half-swing without hitting Savige, then retreated through the stands while Mayhem chased X.

matches.finish: Borealis, the special guest referee, swung a steel chair that he had taken from Octavian and hit Trey Tremendous with it; Rollins covered Trey and Borealis counted the three.
matches.note: Billed as "Tag Team Match - One Fall"; Johnny Borealis was the special guest referee. Borealis paid little attention early, let Octavian choke Trey and pulled him out of the corner, then shoved Octavian off the apron and was slow to see a Rollins cover; he took a steel chair from Octavian and was punched by him, and after Hardy took Octavian over the top rope, Borealis swung the chair and hit Trey (the commentators could not say whether he meant to). Afterwards Hardy and Octavian brawled into the crowd and security separated them.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #22; it is dated 8-25-05 and is billed four days before Annihilation (the fed's title history dates Annihilation 28 August 2005, a Sunday). Joey Andrews announces the entrances. Also on the card: Billed as "Coyle O'Conner vs. Angel"; both men's debuts. Angel, from Loughborough, England, is not tied to a character record, so the match is filed without sides; O'Conner (Newport, Rhode Island, 215 pounds) won. Referee Hal Jenkins explained the rules.

name: WorldWide 24

date.source: the page's own dating (9-8-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: After a flurry that included a Nagata lock and a pedigree, The Marauder hit a Jolly Roger elbow drop on Mayhem and covered him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Bryan Mayhem vs. The Marauder”. The commentators call The Marauder Lexicon under a mask. After the bell Mayhem, furious, took the official by the neck; the finish of the unit is the start of the next segment, in which a video interrupts him.

matches.finish: Almasy threw the birthday cake at Octavian, who caught it; Almasy kicked it into his face with a rising superkick, covered him and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Seymour Almasy vs. Octavian”. An impromptu match: Almasy came out to answer Octavian's challenge and slapped him to start it. Octavian caught Almasy mid-dive and powerbombed him through the Spanish announce table while the referee was distracted by a fight in the front row, then took several covers that Almasy kicked out of. The commentators count the win as Almasy's second in GCW.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-tag-team
matches.finish: With the referee down, Stephens hit both Regulators with a title belt, draped Jake Summers over Blake Cassidy and revived the referee, who counted the three.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Ryan Stephens & Jake Summers vs. The Regulators”; the champions defended against Warz and Blake Cassidy. The Regulators finished Summers with a stunner (the Regulation) but the referee had been knocked down by a Warz lariat meant for Summers. Summers left shaking his head at how Stephens won; the title did not change hands.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.finish: After Knight dived from the turnbuckle and the referee was down, Trey Tremendous set a chair against the ropes and hit a top-rope leg drop on Knight's throat; the referee came to, saw the chair skid across the ring and called for the bell, and Knight kept the title.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Trey Tremendous”. Johnathan Borealis, the United States Champion, sat at the announce table as a guest commentator for the match. Knight backdropped Trey over the top rope onto the security rail, then dived onto Trey and the referee, injuring the same arm that was dislocated at Annihilation. Afterwards Knight smiled at Trey and Borealis could be heard snickering as the show faded. Knight retained the World Heavyweight Title.

matches.finish: After Chrissy-Poo swung a foam hand at him, Aiden Jackson scooped him up into Criminal Justice and covered him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Aiden Jackson vs. Chrissy-Poo”, a first-round match of the Cruiserweight Title Tournament; the announcers call it a debut for both men (line 120: "Both of the participants in this match are making their debuts"). Chrissy-Poo kicked out of three covers (one after a crucifix powerbomb) and hit an enziguri before the finish; afterwards Jackson placed the foam hand over his head.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #24, from Key Arena in Seattle; it is dated 9-8-05 and follows WorldWide 23 (1 September 2005) by a week. Mike Savige comes out as the newly crowned Television Champion, and the commentators bill the three-hour card as the biggest WorldWide yet on the road to FallOut. Two bouts are left unwritten on the page (Dimensioner vs. Meatshield Trainwrecker and Rei Tiu vs. The Rogue Paladin), each with its winner given in brackets. Joey Andrews announces the entrances. Also on the card: A side of this bout, Meatshield Trainwrecker (one of The Guild's two men), is not tied to an individual character record (the unit The Guild is live; neither man has a record of his own), so the bout is filed without sides; Dimensioner keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Dimensioner vs. Meatshield Trainwrecker”. The page itself asks "Anyone want to finish this match?" and gives the winner in square brackets; A side of this bout, Chrissy-poo, is not tied to a character record, so the bout is filed without sides; Aiden Jackson keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Aiden Jackson vs. Chrissy-poo”, a first-round match of the Cruiserweight Title Tournament and the debut of both men. Chrissy-poo opened with a flurry of punches; Jackson took over with a backbreaker, a spinning heel kick, a leg drop from the second rope and a crucifix powerbomb, and Chrissy-poo kicked out three times and landed an enziguri before the finish. The Cruiserweight Title itself was not on the line; A side of this bout, The Rogue Paladin (one of The Guild's two men), is not tied to an individual character record, so the bout is filed without sides; Rei Tiu keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Rei Tiu vs. The Rogue Paladin”, a first-round match of the Cruiserweight Title Tournament. The page gives no account of the match: the bracketed note reads "who wants it? Winner… Rei Tiu!"; A side of this bout, Angel, is not tied to a character record (a bare given name with no GCW record), so the bout is filed without sides; Mike Savige keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Mike Savige vs. Angel”; Savige, the Television Champion, retained and the commentators call it his first defence. Angel led early with an armbar and a reverse atomic drop and lost the match after stopping to pose for the crowd.

name: WorldWide 25

date.source: the page's own dating (9-15-05), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Thunder, hurt by a clothesline, dropped Jones with a small package and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “"The Violence" Vince Jones vs. Ricky Thunder”. Ricky Thunder's GCW debut. After the bell Jones kicked the referee aside and dropped Thunder with an inverted brainbuster (the Silencer), leaving him out cold.

matches.finish: X tripped O'Conner as he went for the Clover, and Jackson caught him in the fall and hit Criminal Justice for the three count.
matches.note: Billed as “Aiden Jackson vs. Coyle O'Conner”, a second-round match of the Cruiserweight Title Tournament; the winner meets Rei Tiu or Zodiac in the final at FallOut. X came through the crowd, threw brass knuckles to Jackson and tripped O'Conner. The Cruiserweight Title itself was not on the line.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.finish: Borealis hit Euthanasia and was about to cover Hardy when Trey Tremendous ran in with a steel chair and hit him; the referee rang the bell for a no contest.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jonathan Borealis vs. Mike Hardy”. Borealis's first defence of the United States Title, as the commentators bill it. Hardy led early and had Borealis hurt; his elbow caught the referee as he rushed in, and Borealis used the moment for a low blow. After the bell Trey kept hitting Borealis with the chair, and when Hardy tapped him on the shoulder, hit Hardy with it too. The card ends the bout with “Winner: No Contest.”; Borealis keeps the title.

matches.finish: Almasy blocked a piledriver, hit a boot and a straightjacket piledriver (Time Compression) and covered Mary for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Seymour Almasy vs. Typhoid Mary”. Mary took a tope con hilo and a fall away slam outside the ring and used a count-out break and a series of pin sequences to stay in it; Almasy stunned her with a palm strike (the "Death Touch") before the finish. The commentators call it nearly a major upset.

matches.finish: Knight, after Savige pulled him out of Marauder's elbow drop, took Marauder down and applied a dragon sleeper; Marauder tapped out and Knight kept the hold until security pulled him off.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Michael “Spitfire” Stevens & The Marauder vs. “The Machine” Mike Savige & LeStatt Knight”. Typhoid Mary walked Knight to the ring. Stevens had cut Savige off from tagging and Marauder had the champion in trouble, but Knight reversed a legsweep into the sleeper; Stevens, who had stopped on the apron, did not help and the commentators read it as intimidation before their FallOut submission match.

notes: The page's own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #25, from General Motors Place in Vancouver; it is dated 9-15-05 and follows WorldWide 24 by a week. The commentators put FallOut "two weeks" away and name Rei Tiu's tournament match with Zodiac for "next week". Joey Andrews announces the entrances. Also on the card: A side of this bout, Gabriel White, is not tied to a character record (a debut with no record in the wing), so the bout is filed without sides; X keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Gabriel White vs. X”. White won by count-out in his debut. Ms. Scabbia was at ringside with X; just before the ten count Coyle O'Conner came over the guardrail with a steel chair, hit X in the spine and ran back through the crowd; A side of this bout, "Poe" Dunn, is not tied to a character record (a debut with no record in the wing), so the bout is filed without sides; Donny Diamond keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Donny Diamond vs. “Poe” Dunn”; both men were new to GCW. Dunn took an early lead with a hip toss and elbow drops but argued with the referee over a count; Diamond won.

name: WorldWide 26

date.source: Circa: the page prints no date; it numbers itself Episode #26, between WorldWide 25 (dated 9-15-05) and FallOut (dated Thursday, 29 September 2005), whose own text calls this show's events "last week"; donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Rei Tiu dodged Zodiac's single-leg crab and rolled her up in a small package for the three count.
matches.note: Billed as “Zodiac vs. Rei Tiu”, a second-round match of the Cruiserweight Title Tournament; Rei Tiu goes on to meet Aiden Jackson in the final at FallOut. The Cruiserweight Title itself was not on the line. Zodiac got a shoulder up from a falling powerbomb at the last instant before three; Rei then missed his somersault leg drop (the Blackout) and Zodiac went for her single-leg crab (the Annihilator), which he turned into the winning small package.

matches.finish: With the referee down, a steel chair thrown from ringside hit Trey in the corner; Almasy climbed back to the top rope and hit a Shooting Star Press for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Trey Tremendous vs. Seymour Almasy”. The commentators put Almasy's winning streak at three going in and call him undefeated after it. Trey kicked the referee into the ropes as Almasy climbed; when the chair hit Trey, Borealis, smiling, slid off the apron and walked to the back. As the ring announcer began the announcement, Rich Rollins came out and superkicked Almasy, then held a figure four on his knee while the referee tried to pull him away; Rollins and Almasy meet at FallOut.

matches.finish: Stevens snapped Jason down in a reverse Fujiwara armbar and Jason tapped out at once; time three seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Michael Stevens vs. Jason”. Round one of the Submission Lock Challenge: Michael Stevens takes on the job-squad man Jason and LeStatt Knight takes on Phyl, each side applying a submission, and the man who makes his opponent tap out in the least time wins. Jason and Phyl came out in job-squad fashion; referee Josh Briggs worked all six bouts and Typhoid Mary walked Knight to the ring. This one lasted three seconds.

matches.finish: Phyl asked to be let out; Knight locked a dragon sleeper, Phyl shouted for help and referee Briggs called for the bell; time three seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Phyl”. Round two, a tie with the first bout at three seconds; Stevens insisted on another attempt.

matches.finish: Stevens held Jason in a stalling vertical suplex, dropped him and applied a figure four; Jason tapped out; time thirty-eight seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Michael Stevens vs. Jason”. Round three: Stevens deliberately drew the match out for effect.

matches.finish: Knight put Phyl through a middle-rope death valley driver and two powerbombs and then locked a Boston crab; Phyl tapped; time thirty-eight seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Phyl”. Round four: Knight matched Stevens's thirty-eight seconds and the commentators credit him with timing it.

matches.finish: Stevens threw Jason into the corner, climbed with him and dived off in an armbar; Jason tapped out; time thirteen seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Michael Stevens vs. Jason”. Round five: the referee tried to stop Stevens and was stared down.

matches.finish: Knight locked the dragon sleeper again but Stevens, under the ring apron, hooked Phyl's foot on the ropes twice; Knight then wrapped Phyl's neck and foot together and the referee called for the bell; time twenty-seven seconds.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Phyl”. Round six. The page prints the announcement of the time but not Phyl's submission itself: the referee calls for the bell after Knight's hold. Michael Stevens, with the lowest time (thirteen seconds against twenty-seven), was announced the winner of the Submission Lock Challenge; Typhoid Mary chased him up the ramp and the crowd joined him in mocking Knight.

matches.finish: After an Acid Drop got only a two count, Chrissy-Poo rolled Dimensioner up from behind, holding the tights, and got the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Dimensioner vs. Chrissy-poo”, the opening bout; the announcers recall that Chrissy-Poo had lost to Aiden Jackson two weeks before. Chrissy-Poo came out from under the ring and hit Dimensioner with a banana.

notes: The page prints no date. Its own heading numbers it WorldWide Episode #26, from Calgary; it follows WorldWide 25 (15 September 2005), which names Rei Tiu's match with Zodiac for "next week", and the FallOut card, dated Thursday, 29 September 2005, looks back on this show's events as "last week". The commentators here count FallOut as "three days away" and "this Sunday", which the FallOut card's own date does not bear out. Joey Andrews announces the entrances. Also on the card: A side of this bout, Chrissy-poo, is not tied to a character record, so the bout is filed without sides; Dimensioner keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Dimensioner vs. Chrissy-poo”; Chrissy-poo's first win in GCW. He started with a banana thrown from under the ring, mooned the crowd, and kicked into Dimensioner's head the chair Dimensioner had taken from announcer James Bryan; the page prints the lyrics of Dimensioner's entrance song at the top of the bout; A side of this bout, Angel, is not tied to a character record (a bare given name with no GCW record), so the bout is filed without sides; Ricky Thunder keeps his match appearance row. Billed as “Ricky Thunder vs. Angel”; Thunder's interview earlier on the card shows him in a neck brace from Vince Jones's attack the week before. Referee Hal Jenkins worked it; Angel led with clotheslines, a sidewalk slam, a springboard moonsault and a choke slam, and Thunder came back with an inverted STF, a cloverleaf and a cross face chicken wing before the finish; A side of this bout, Meatshield Trainwrecker (one of The Guild's two men), is not tied to an individual character record, so the bout is filed without sides; Mike Savige keeps his match appearance row. Billed as ““The Machine” Mike Savige vs. Meatshield Trainwrecker”; Savige, the Television Champion, retained. Savige controlled the early going; Trainwrecker came back outside the ring with a suplex and an elbow drop, and while The Marauder ran down the ramp and argued with Savige at ringside, Trainwrecker charged Savige from behind and then powerbombed him in the ring.

name: Devil's Night 2005

date.source: the page's own dating (Sunday, October 30th, 2005), donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Sam Wolack vs. Coyle O’Conner”, a falls-count-anywhere singles match. The page carries no account of it: under its heading it reads only "Still waiting on this one…", so no result is given. Bryan's introduction names it the opening bout.

matches.finish: Before the bell, a man in a hooded sweatshirt from the crowd (Peter Maxwell, The Dark Messiah) beat Hardy down and hit him with a High Impact Piledriver; Caldera Mask then hit a Strong Sambo Suplex and put a foot on him as Senior Referee Tony Salazar counted "One. Two. Duh."
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Hardy vs. Caldera Mask”. Dan Rivero escorted Caldera Mask and rang the bell himself. Hardy was attacked on the way to the ring and never got to fight back; the attacker pulled off his hood and was Peter Maxwell, who is banned from GCW buildings. The count is printed "One. Two. Duh." and no ring announcement follows, so the pinfall to Caldera Mask rests on the commentary ("Salazar has no choice but to count Hardy for the pinfall") and on Rivero ringing the bell again. Afterwards Caldera Mask and Rivero turned on Maxwell, Caldera Mask holding him in a crossface chickenwing while Rivero kicked him, and Rivero named Mike Savige as their next target.

matches.finish: Toxic hit The Marauder with the Toxic Waste and hooked the leg for the three count after a barbed-wire baseball bat to the face; The Marauder, bleeding through his mask, challenged Toxic again afterwards until medics tackled him and gave him an injection.
matches.note: Billed on the page as "The Marauder vs. The Mystery Assailant"; the opponent turns out to be Toxic, returning, whom the commentary and The Marauder tie to four weeks of attacks on The Marauder. Announced as a hardcore match. The ring announcer's "Here is your winner-" is cut off by The Marauder.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.finish: Eva hit a Super Hurricanrana off the top rope and was counted the winner, but referee David Fellows, shown a replay of Erik VanLorne standing below Borealis, reversed his decision and awarded the match to Borealis by disqualification.
matches.note: Billed on the page as "United States Championship Match – One Fall: Jonathan Borealis vs. Eva VanLorne". Borealis's candy-and-free-food promo opens the bout; Erik VanLorne escorted his sister and stood at ringside. The commentators insist Erik never touched Borealis. The announcer first calls Eva the NEW GCW United States Champion, then gives Borealis the match by disqualification as STILL champion.

matches.finish: Almasy turned Rollins's top-rope superplex into a top-rope reverse stunner and both men lay out; Almasy crawled to within inches of Rollins but collapsed, Briggs counted ten and called for the bell, and the announcer declared the match a DRAW.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Rich "The Renegade" Rollins vs. Seymour Almasy”. Their first meeting, at FallOut, "ended quickly and without a winner". Rollins kicked out of Almasy's guillotine legdrop, and Almasy kicked out of Rollins's piledriver and Anarchist Elbow and broke his Sharpshooter; Rollins superkicked Almasy out of the air as he came off the top rope. The commentators call Almasy undefeated in GCW before this match. Almasy walked out under his own power; Rollins was helped from the ring.

matches.finish: RipeFist, unmasked by then as Michael “Spitfire” Stevens, turned Savige's guerilla press into an Inferno DDT into the last open grave and buried him with the bulldozer to win the number-one contendership.

eliminations.note: buried alive when Chrissy-Poo pushed the dirt into the grave with a bulldozer, after a low blow and an Acid Drop facebuster into the grave
buried alive by Rei Tiu with a bulldozer after a Frankensteiner into the grave and a Blackout legdrop onto him
hit by Aiden Jackson's bulldozer into a grave and buried alive, after Aiden had already hit him with a shovel
buried alive by Mike Savige with a bulldozer after the Machinehead
buried alive by RipeFist, who had unmasked as Michael Stevens, with a bulldozer after a counter into an Inferno DDT in the grave

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Main Event: 6-Man Buried Alive Match, GCW #1 Contendership: Aiden Jackson vs. Bryan Mayhem vs. Chrissy-Poo vs. Mike Savige vs. Rei Tiu vs. RipeFist”. Six entrants; Chrissy-Poo, who entered by winning the costume contest at WorldWide that week, is Manalishi (billed Chrissy-Poo). A participant is eliminated when placed in a grave and completely covered with dirt. LeStatt Knight and Typhoid Mary watch from thrones above the graveyard. Late in the match RipeFist unwrapped his bandages and was revealed as Michael “Spitfire” Stevens, and Knight ordered him to "DESTROY HIM!"; the ring announcer names Michael “Spitfire” Stevens as the winner and new number-one contender, who will challenge Knight at NC-17.

notes: The page dates itself Sunday, October 30th, 2005, at Joe Louis Arena in Detroit, Michigan, and its commentary calls the main event the main event of "Devil's Night 2005"; the fed's own record held no card for this night, which is not the 2001 Devil's Night. The champions it names agree with the fed's title histories for the day: LeStatt Knight World Champion from 28 July 2005, Bryan Mayhem Television Champion from 27 October 2005 and Johnny Borealis United States Champion from 28 August 2005. Joey Andrews announces the entrances.

name: FallOut 2005

date.source: Circa: the fed's own advance card bills “FallOut Sunday, September 25th 2005 LIVE on X:TV” and WorldWide 25 and 26 count down to that Sunday, while this page prints “Live on X:TV Thursday, September 29 2005”; donated by GCW's founder, 2026-10-06 (an e-mail donation)

matches.finish: Joshua Curtis set Blake Cassidy on Ami Mizuno's shoulders and Mizuno dived off the top turnbuckle with the Sibling Superbomb; Curtis covered for the three count while Mizuno baseball-slid Warz out of the ring.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “The Regulators vs. The Bloodlines”: the number one contenders' match for the GCW Tag Team Titles and the first GCW match of The Bloodlines, Joshua Curtis and his sister Ami Mizuno. The Regulators are Blake Cassidy and Warz. Before the finish Curtis pulled down the top rope and sent Warz to the floor. The commentary says the winners “get to face whoever comes out of the Guild/Double S title match later tonight”.

matches.finish: Aiden Jackson ran in and tripped the referee; Coyle DDT'd Jackson onto a chair, hit X with the chair, and covered him for the three count when the referee got back in the ring.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Coyle O'Conner vs. X”, and listed in the contents as “Impromptu Match”. Coyle had been reported unfit to wrestle with a broken arm and his match with X called off; he came out unannounced, said no doctor had cleared him, and challenged X, who answered, while a second X appeared in the ring behind Coyle. Coyle gave X his own finisher, the X-Buster, for a near fall before Aiden Jackson's run-in.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-tag-team
matches.finish: With Stephens gone, Joshua Curtis set Jake Summers over Ami Mizuno's shoulders again and Mizuno hit a second Sibling Superbomb from the top; Curtis covered Summers for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jake Summers & Ryan Stephens vs. The Guild”, for the Tag Team Titles. The Guild missed their cue and never appeared. Tiffany came out instead, put it to Stephens that the champions must defend against the number one contenders and asked whether he liked working for GCW, and named The Bloodlines the challengers; Stephens hit them both with a double face crusher on the way to the ring. It was The Bloodlines' second match of the night. Stephens, who the commentary says was doing everything he could to lose, pulled his hand away from Summers's tag, gave him the finger and walked out of the arena. The Bloodlines were handed the titles and announced as the NEW GCW Tag Team Champions on their first night in the company.

matches.finish: Octavian stormed the referee after a three count was nullified by Hardy's foot on the rope and raised a chair; the referee took it away, Hardy caught Octavian's kick, reversed it into Octavian's own submission hold, the Roman Rapper, and Octavian tapped out.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Mike Hardy vs. Octavian”; the advance card billed it a Grudge Match, the commentary calls it a bitter rivalry to settle, and no title was on the line. Pete calls Octavian a three-time World Champion. Octavian spent the early minutes outside the ring while Hardy used his speed; Hardy locked in an armbar choke, and Octavian came back with a surfboard stretch, a dragon suplex and an STF. Octavian's Roman Devastator got a three count, but the referee had seen Hardy's foot on the rope.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-cruiserweight
matches.finish: Aiden Jackson hit a Shooting Star Press for a near fall, then lifted Rei Tiu onto his shoulders for Criminal Justice and pinned him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Rei Tiu vs. Aiden Jackson”: the final of the GCW Cruiserweight Title Tournament, for the Cruiserweight Title. Jackson reached it past Chrissy-Poo and Coyle O'Conner, Tiu past the Rogue Paladin and Zodiac. Referee Josh Briggs showed the belt to both men before the bell. Jackson was announced as the NEW GCW Cruiserweight champion, and the crowd gave Tiu a standing ovation.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-hdtv
matches.finish: A black Lincoln, its driver unseen, ran The Marauder down and sped away; Savige pulled the referee aside and got a two count, then hooked the Machinehead on the pavement and pinned him for the three count.
matches.note: Billed as ““The Machine” Mike Savige vs. The Marauder”: a Parking Lot Brawl for the Television Championship, fought among parked cars with no disqualification; the rules, read out by Briggs (printed “Brigg”), let a pin or submission count only inside a square painted on the ground. Eva walked The Marauder out, and James Bryan calls him “The Marauder, Johnny Lexicon”. The Marauder put a boot through a car window and ripped the muffler off a car, then stood over Savige with the muffler raised and threw it aside, and the Lincoln hit him. Savige kept the Television Title; Eva and two EMTs ran to The Marauder afterwards.

matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-united-states
matches.finish: With Trey Tremendous taken out injured, Borealis caught Eva in a German suplex and held her shoulders down for the three count.

eliminations.note: helped from the ring by paramedics with a possible knee injury after Borealis pulled him off the top turnbuckle and he fell to the floor; referee Timothy Vale ruled the move not a disqualification and the match went on between the other two

matches.note: Billed on the card as “Jonathan Borealis vs. Eva VanLorne vs. Trey Tremendous”, for the United States Title (the page prints Borealis as Jonathan and Johnathan); Borealis, the champion, kept the title. The advance card billed Borealis against Eva alone, and the commentary calls Trey the last-minute entry. Trey offered Eva a game of Rock Paper Scissors to settle who went first, and she ran at Borealis instead. Trey and Eva fought Borealis together until Eva pushed Trey off a pin, and her frogsplash later got a near fall on Trey. When Trey fell to the floor, Eva, enraged, went after Borealis, and he ended it with a German suplex.

matches.finish: On the top rope Rollins tried to superplex Almasy to the floor; Almasy pulled him off his feet and dived back, superplexing Rollins through the announce table, and referee Timothy Vale signalled for the bell. The match was called off as a no contest.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “Rich “The Renegade” Rollins vs. Seymour Almasy”. The commentary says Rollins had hardly been seen since Almasy came to challenge him at Annihilation, that he returned on WorldWide the week before to beat Almasy down, and that Almasy was undefeated in GCW, five wins and no losses; the advance card billed it a Grudge Match. On his way in Rollins superkicked a fan's “ROLLINS FEARS ALMASY” sign; Almasy picked up the torn halves, held them together and showed the message to the crowd. Both men shoved referee Timothy Vale aside at once. The superplex crushed Pete and The Jhub under Rollins at the announce table, while Almasy missed the table and landed on the floor mats. Four stretchers were brought; Almasy slid off his and the two fought again, over the guardrail and up the stairs through the crowd, until Almasy staggered out of the cameras' view and Rollins followed, with head referee Josh Briggs and the officials in pursuit. The page prints “Winner: No Contest”.

matches.stipulation: Submission Match (World Heavyweight Championship, no disqualification)
matches.title: gcw-gcwonline-2001-world-heavyweight
matches.finish: Stevens held Knight in a Reverse Fujiwara Armbar until Knight's arm dropped three times for referee Josh Briggs; Knight then flipped over, turned it into the dragon sleeper, and Stevens tapped out.
matches.note: Billed on the card as “LeStatt Knight vs. Michael “Spitfire” Stevens”: a Submission Match for the World Heavyweight Championship, the main event, with no disqualifications; only a tap out could end it. The two used chairs, the steel steps, two tables and a kendo stick. Stevens crushed Knight's left arm under the steel steps, and the commentary calls the arm broken; Knight wrestled on with it. When Briggs dropped Knight's arm the third time the crowd roared, but Knight surged up and countered; David Yale, back on commentary, says on the replay that Knight “played possum”. After the bell Typhoid Mary helped Knight up the ramp while EMTs put a neck brace on Stevens. Knight kept the World Heavyweight Title.

notes: The fed's own advance card for this show, on its site in October 2005, bills it “FallOut Sunday, September 25th 2005 LIVE on X:TV”, and WorldWide 25 and 26 count down to that Sunday (“the man you have to face in ten days”, “three days away”, “this Sunday”). This page, the show itself, prints “Live on X:TV Thursday, September 29 2005” and calls the events of WorldWide 26 “last week”, and WorldWide 27 opens “Just one week ago we witnessed FallOut”. The date is filed as about 25 September 2005, the billed Sunday; the page keeps its own date. It is from Toronto and names no venue. Devil's Night (Sunday, 30 October, Salt Lake City) and NC-17 (Sunday, 27 November, Madison Square Garden) are promoted from ringside. Steven Caldera, the Owner and President, tells the crowd he is leaving GCW television, names Tiffany York the authority backstage and brings David Yale back to call the main event. Joey Andrews announces the entrances. This is not the FallOut of 2001. Also on the card: “Bryan Mayhem vs. Gabriel White” (Singles Match – One Fall), the first match of the card. Twelve cloaked men carrying candles ringed the ring for Mayhem's entrance. White busted Mayhem open on the ring post. Referee Hal Jenkins called for a microphone to ask Pete for a hot dog, sat on the top turnbuckle while both men lay still, and later ate a hot dog at the announce table while the two climbed a ladder set up outside the ring. The commentary says that one of the men “managed to cover the other, but it couldn't have been on purpose”; the ring announcer named Mayhem the winner.

date.source: Circa: the card was posted to the PTC forum on 8 October 2006 for “This Week”, the first WorldWide after Dangerous Games (25 September 2006 in this wing), and prints “Thursday, September 12th”; 12 September 2006 was a Tuesday and falls before Dangerous Games, while Thursday the 12th of that week is 12 October 2006, so the printed month is read as a slip.

notes: Announced on the PTC forum on 8 October 2006 as WorldWide #53, “The Road to NC-17”, from Phoenix, Arizona, the first step to NC-17. Only the announced card survives; the results of the night are not held. The fed's own title history dates Bryan Mayhem's Television Championship win, the match this card bills against Jordan White, to a WorldWide of 19 October 2006, a week after this card's own date.
